Iran and Ceasefire U.S. and Iran announce a deal: The United States and Iran reached an initial agreement early Monday to extend the ceasefire for 60 days and open the Strait of Hormuz. Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif told the National Assembly in Islamabad: "After three months and 16 days of unparalleled trials, the immediate and permanent cessation of military operations has been announced across all fronts, including Iran, America and Lebanon." The signing is set for Friday in Switzerland, with U.S. Vice President JD Vance saying he plans to attend and leaving open the possibility Trump could as well. President Donald Trump announced the deal in a on Truth Social, saying, "The Deal with the Islamic Republic of Iran is now complete. Congratulations to all! I hereby fully authorize the toll free opening of the Strait of Hormuz, and, simultaneously herewith, authorize the immediate removal of the United States Naval blockade. Ships of the World, start your engines. Let the oil flow!" Trump on Monday that vessels were already beginning to move through the Strait of Hormuz, writing on Truth Social, "Ships are starting to move, many loaded up with Oil, out of the Strait of Hormuz. They are going along the Southern "Highway," which is totally safe, secure, and pristine. There are other areas of travel, also!!!" Iran's deputy foreign minister, Kazem Gharibabadi, confirmed the deal on state television but said implementation would not begin until Friday's signing, while Iranian state television cited the Supreme National Security Council saying the war "will end immediately and permanently beginning tonight" and that the U.S. naval blockade "will be terminated immediately and in full." The MOU faces significant hurdles. It gives just 60 days to resolve Iran's stockpile of highly enriched uranium and its nuclear program--issues that took years to negotiate in the 2015 deal. The leaders of the E4--Britain, France, Germany, and Italy--announced Sunday they were prepared to lift sanctions on Iran contingent on verifiable steps toward curtailing its nuclear program, according to Reuters, while welcoming the U.S.-Iran memorandum of understanding. Lebanon included in deal, Israel pushes back The spokesperson for Iran's Foreign Ministry, Esmaeil Baghaei, reiterated on Monday that Lebanon is a critical part of the MOU with the U.S. "Respecting the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Lebanon is part of the interim agreement with the US," Baghaei told reporters, according to Al Jazeera. Lebanese President Joseph Aoun the announcement of a U.S.-Iran memorandum of understanding, saying he followed it "with interest" and that it includes a commitment to "stop military operations and escalation in the region, including Lebanon." He said Lebanon "values what this memorandum contains in terms of respect for Lebanese specificity," stressing that stability in Lebanon is "an integral part of any serious effort to entrench stability in the region." Hezbollah also issued a statement welcoming the agreement, congratulating Iran on what it described as a "great achievement" of securing a "comprehensive ceasefire on all fronts, including Lebanon." The group also said Lebanon should "make good use of this regional and international umbrella" to achieve sovereignty and "liberate its land within national unity." Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz insisted on Monday that Israeli troops won't withdraw from land seized in Lebanon. "Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and I are pursuing a clear policy under which the [military] will remain in the security zones in Lebanon, Syria and Gaza for an unlimited period of time in order to protect the border and Israeli communities from there against jihadist elements," Katz said in a statement. He added that the areas would be "cleared of local residents" and that "all terror infrastructure" will be destroyed. Katz said he had conveyed Israel's position to US officials, and warned that "if Iran attacks Israel because of events in Lebanon, we will strike it with full force." Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reportedly President Donald Trump on Sunday that Israel does not consider itself bound by the Lebanon-related provisions of the emerging U.S.-Iran agreement and will not withdraw from positions it currently occupies inside Lebanese territory, with Israeli forces to continue military operations against Hezbollah regardless of any Washington-Tehran understandings, according to reports in Yedioth Ahronoth and Maariv. Three senior Iranian officials vowed retaliation against Israel after Beirut strike: The U.S.-Iran agreement appeared at risk on early Sunday after Israel bombed the southern suburbs of Beirut.** The strike, which hit an apartment building in Dahiyeh, killed three people--a father, mother, and their daughter--and wounded 16, Lebanon's Health Ministry said. Three of Iran's most senior officials of a forceful response, with parliament speaker and lead negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf writing that Israel would never "isolate and pick off any part of the Axis of Resistance" and adding an idiomatic warning translating to "you made your move, and we'll answer in kind." Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr declared that "the response of the warriors of Islam is forthcoming," calling Lebanon "our lifeblood" and warning that any crossing of Iran's red lines "will not be tolerated," while Supreme Leader adviser and former acting president Mohammad Mokhber called the pattern of American diplomacy paired with Israeli strikes "repetitive and unacceptable," writing that "in defending Lebanon, we will show no courtesies to anyone." Trump publicly scolds Netanyahu over Lebanon strike: President Donald Trump on Sunday that an Israeli strike on Lebanon the day the Iran deal was announced "should not have happened, particularly on a special day when we are so close to a Peace Deal with Iran." Trump reportedly told Axios he confronted Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu directly--"Why did Bibi have to do a fucking attack? I was so pissed off. He has no fucking judgement. I let him know that." Trump al told Fox News he asked Netanyahu "what the fck are you doing?" before ordering no further strikes and saying he would ask Iran not to retaliate. Tanker struck near Oman: A tanker was by an "unknown projectile" near the Strait of Hormuz, about six nautical miles east of Oman, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Centre reported on Saturday. No injuries or environmental damage were reported, and the tanker continued onto its next port of call. Burial date announced for Khameinei: Former Supreme Leader Ali Khameinei will be on July 9th in the northeastern city of Mashhad, Iranian State Television announced on Saturday, following six days of ceremonies beginning on the 4th. He was killed by an Israeli strike on his residence on February 28. Lebanon Killed and wounded: At least 3,783 people have been killed, and 11,699 wounded, in Israeli attacks on Lebanon since March 2, according to the Lebanese Health Ministry. Israeli attacks persist across southern Lebanon on Monday: An Israeli drone a vehicle in Kfartebnit, killing one person, according to the state's National News Agency (NNA). Press TV journalist Hadi Hoteit was in Kfartebnit, southern Lebanon, after Israeli shelling struck nearby, according to NNA. He is undergoing surgery for shrapnel in his foot at a hospital in Nabatieh. Israeli artillery also shelled the towns of Nabatieh al-Fawqa. The Israeli army carried out demolition operations in the southern Lebanese town of Khiam. Israel conducts strikes, orders displacement in Lebanon over the weekend: An Israeli strike on Douweir killed a Lebanese chef in the southern village of Douweir on Sunday, Press TV correspondent Hadi Hoteit . The Israeli military its controlled detonation of homes in the southern Lebanese towns of Haddatha, Khiam, Markaba, and Kfar Tebnit on Sunday. The Israeli military also the forced displacement of 24 villages across southern Lebanon on Saturday, ordering residents in the Nabatieh, Jezzine, and Sidon districts to flee north of the Zahrani River in anticipation of strikes. A Lebanese soldier was seriously wounded by an Israeli strike in Nabatieh, according to a statement from the country's military. The statement said that the same soldier was targeted near Al-Najda Hospital before being struck on his motorcycle, in what it described as another of Israel's "double-tap" strikes in the country. An Israeli missile strike on Saturday Ali Badih Hussein, the current Mukhtar (elected village head) of Rihane, a village in southern Lebanon, according to L'Orient Today. A former Mukhtar of Riahane, Ismail Abdullah, was killed in a separate attack on Saturday, as he watered plants outside of his home. Hezbollah responds, hits northern Israel: Two suspected Hezbollah drones an Israeli military zone in the Western Galilee near the Lebanese border early Sunday with no injuries reported, the Israeli military reported. Hezbollah also a wave of operations against Israeli forces across southern Lebanon on Sunday, including rocket barrages and FPV attacks on Israeli military positions and armored vehicles. Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich by calling on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to invoke the Dahiya doctrine--Israel's strategy of using disproportionate force against civilian infrastructure, named for the Beirut suburb Israel leveled in 2006--writing that Netanyahu should "demolish buildings in Dahiya today." Palestine Killed and wounded: Over the last 24 hours, seven Palestinians were killed--six in new attacks and one recovered from under the rubble--and six were injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,003 killed, with 173,252 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 992 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 3,144, while 784 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. Israel kills five, including two children, on Monday: At least five Palestinians, including two children, were killed in Israeli attacks across the Gaza Strip on Monday, according to WAFA. A nurse at Al-Shifa Hospital and his child were , and several others wounded, some critically, when an Israeli drone struck a home in the Sheikh Radwan neighborhood, north of Gaza City.** The body of another child arrived at Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital alongside his wounded father, after Israeli forces opened fire on them Sunday and detained them in the Wadi al-Salqa area, central Gaza. A separate drone strike on Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza killed one person, while a woman was earlier in the day in al-Zawaida. Israeli attacks on Gaza over the weekend: At least nine Palestinians were in continuing Israeli attacks across Gaza on Sunday, including a 15-year-old shot by Israeli gunfire east of Khan Younis, according to Shehab News. Six people were killed in an Israeli airstrike on a warehouse near Al-Yemen Al-Saeed Hospital in the Jabalia refugee camp in northern Gaza on Sunday. An Israeli drone strike a group of Palestinians southwest of Al-Nuseirat refugee camp in the central Gaza Strip on Sunday, wounding at least three people Hamas submits unified Palestinian factions ' response to a second phase of Trump Gaza deal: Hamas it has delivered a formal unified response from Palestinian factions to the roadmap for implementing the second phase of President Donald Trump's Gaza proposal, following a week of meetings in Cairo involving Hamas, other factions, and mediators from Egypt, Qatar, and Turkey. The talks produced what Hamas called a "unified national position" presented to mediators on Friday, which calls for full implementation of the first phase--particularly its humanitarian protocol and a complete cessation of aggression--as well as entry of the Gaza Administrative Committee, a full Israeli withdrawal, and reconstruction leading to Palestinian statehood and self-determination. Hamas said its delegation will remain in Cairo for further talks. Israeli settlers burn vehicles, attempt to set mosque ablaze near Ramallah: Israeli settlers the village of Burqa, east of Ramallah in the occupied West Bank on Sunday evening, setting fire to a vehicle and attempting to burn down a mosque, according to WAFA. Witnesses said settlers torched a vehicle parked near Al-Nour Mosque, causing material damage, before breaking the mosque's doors and setting a fire at its entrance. Residents managed to extinguish the flames before they spread inside the building, while the attackers fled the area. The incident came shortly after another settler attack in the nearby town of Deir Dibwan, where two vehicles were burned and two others vandalized. The Palestinian Foreign Ministry condemned the attacks, saying they were part of a "systematic Israeli policy" that uses "organized, daily terrorism" against Palestinians with the aim of displacing them from their land. Palestinian prisoner Imad Sarhan dies in Gilboa Prison: Imad Rajih Sarhan, 47, from Haifa, in Israel's Gilboa Prison after suffering a heart attack, the Palestinian Prisoners' Affairs Commission and Palestinian Prisoners' Club announced, saying years of torture, medical neglect, and repeated solitary confinement had left him with chronic heart and vascular disease, high blood pressure, and wheelchair dependency since his imprisonment began in 2001. The organizations said Sarhan is the 90th Palestinian prisoner to die since the start of Israel's war on Gaza and the 327th documented death in Israeli custody since 1967, with rights groups describing Israel's prison system as carrying out a policy of "slow executions" through torture, starvation, and medical neglect. More than 9,400 Palestinians remain held in Israeli prisons, including 4,640 without charge or trial. Sister of Dr. Hussam Abu Safiyah says he lost half his body weight in detention: Samahir Abu Safiyah told Drop Site News that her brother, pediatrician and Kamal Adwan Hospital director Dr. Hussam Abu Safiyah, appeared unrecognizable when he was brought before the Israeli High Court this week after more than 500 days in detention without charge. Family lawyers reported he has lost roughly half his body weight, suffers deteriorating eyesight, contracted scabies, and remains held in solitary confinement at Nafha Prison. Dr. Abu Safiyah, who continued treating patients at Kamal Adwan after Israeli forces killed his son in 2024 described his imprisonment to the court as "unjust and arbitrary," while his sister said bruises visible on his hands and his aged appearance indicated torture. "His only crime was staying in the hospital for the sake of the children, the injured, and the wounded," Samahir said, calling on the world to demand his immediate release. Her interview is. U.S. News By Julian Andreone, with Ryan Grim. Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email Andreone at. Denver Venues Shut Down Hasan Piker Political Rallies, Dub Them "Neo-Nazi": A rally planned for Sunday, which was supposed to feature streamer Hasan Piker along with Democratic House challenger Melat Kiros and Senate challenger Julie Gonzales , was blocked after pressure on various venues, including the Ogden Theatre, Reelworks, and Stanley Marketplace, which all canceled despite having signed contracts, The rally was moved to the state Capitol steps later that day. Deep Singh Badhesha , an event organizer, all three venues canceled after deposits were paid, with Stanley Marketplace telling him he was told it was "a neo-Nazi rally." The pressure to cancel, he said, appeared highly coordinated, and subsequent venues he called told him they had been warned not to host the rally. "You didn't tell me it was a neo-Nazi rally," the final venue to cancel told Badhesha. The speakers would make for an odd lineup at a Nazi rally: aside from the Turkish-American Muslim Piker, Representatives Justin Pearson and Donavan McKinney were also scheduled to speak and are both Black; Gonzales is Latina and Kiros emigrated from Tigray, Ethiopia. Gonzales is challenging incumbent Sen. John Hickenlooper. The primary will be on June 30. Washington, DC and Oklahoma host primaries Tuesday: In DC, DSA-backed Janeese Lewis George is poised to become mayor. Trump has to take the city over if she wins. In Oklahoma, voters will have the opportunity to more than the minimum wage to $15/hour. Stanford students walk out of Sundar Pichai commencement address: An estimated 100 to 200 Stanford students of Google CEO Sundar Pichai 's commencement address Sunday, chanting "Free, free Palestine" as boos and cries of "shame on you" came from parts of the crowd. The protest was in response to Google's Project Nimbus cloud contract with the Israeli government, which includes services for Israel's Defense Ministry and other state agencies. Republicans Push SAVE Act: President Donald Trump and Sen. Mike Lee continue mounting a pressure campaign to pass the SAVE America Act before the 2026 midterms. The bill would impose significant restrictions on access to voting. Senate Majority LeaderJohn Thune has already made it clear the bill does not have enough votes to pass the Senate and has thus opted against bringing it to the floor. Trump has asserted he will not sign a FISA reauthorization unless it is coupled with the SAVE Act. Now, House GOP leaders are seeking to skirt obstacles in the Senate by including portions of the legislation in their reconciliation bill, according to Politico. Other International News Appeals court upholds UK ban on Palestine Action: An appeals court in London on Monday upheld a UK government ban on activist group Palestine Action as a "terrorist group," overturning a decision by a lower court. The ban was first imposed on July 5, 2025, under Britain's Terrorism Act and more than 3,000 arrests linked to support for Palestine Action have been made since. The group challenged the ban in court on the basis that it was "disproportionate" and had a "very significant" impact on human rights. In February the High Court in London ruled in Palestine Action's favor. Monday's ruling at the Appeals court however reverses that judgement. Amnesty International called the verdict "deeply disappointing," on X: "The banning of Palestine Action as a terrorist organisation is a grave misuse of counter-terrorism powers with serious consequences for human rights." The ruling came after a judge on Friday sentenced four Palestine Action activists to years in prison as terrorists over their involvement in a 2024 protest and raid on a factory operated by one of Israel's largest arms manufacturers, Elbit. The prison sentences range from four to over seven years. The four defendants must also legally register to a law enforcement terrorist surveillance system for 15 years following their release from prison. Hegseth announces expanded U.S. military strikes across Latin America: War Secretary Pete Hegseth Sunday on CBS's Face the Nation that Americans "should expect" U.S. military strikes in countries including Ecuador and Guatemala as part of a new "America's Counter Cartel Coalition" formed with partner governments across Central and South America to "defeat and destroy." The announcement followed President Donald Trump's announcement that a U.S. strike killed Tren de Aragua leader Hector Guerrero Flores, known as Niño Guerrero, on June 12 in Venezuela's Bolivar state. UN: Drone strikes kill over 1,000 civilians in Sudan in first five months of 2026: More than 1,000 civilians have been in drone strikes in Sudan between January and May 2026, a senior UN human rights official said, warning of a sharp escalation in the war's brutality. UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk said there has been a "sharp increase" in drone attacks alongside widespread reports of rape and sexual violence, as the war enters its fourth year. At least 2,670 people, including civilians and combatants, were killed in 2025, marking a 600% increase in drone-related deaths, according to ACLED data. This statement follows a recent strike by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) that killed at least 15 people in el-Obeid, after drones hit a cemetery and a gas station, health officials said. Gunmen kill 17 farmers in northwestern Nigeria 's Zamfara state: Gunmen at least 17 farmers and wounded 13 others as they worked their fields Friday in the Maradun area of Zamfara state, as part of the state's recent surge in attacks by armed bandits. Friday's attack came one day after gunmen abducted 39 people in a nearby Maradun community while residents were meeting to negotiate over kidnappings. Doctors Without Borders investigation finds widespread staff sexual abuse of Sudanese refugees: A confidential Doctors Without Borders investigation 59 allegations of sexual abuse and exploitation by aid workers in camps hosting Sudanese refugees in eastern Chad, including claims that staff traded food, jobs, and humanitarian assistance for sex, with some victims reportedly underage girls, the AP reported. MSF dismissed 18 staff members following the inquiry, with investigators noting that some cases suggested possible organized sexual trafficking. Geneva protests ahead of G7 Summit: Geneva police fired teargas at protesters after a demonstration against the upcoming G7 summit in neighboring France. Around 20,000 people marched peacefully before police allege some participants attacked a parked Tesla and a United Nations office. The summit will be held from June 15-17 in Evian-les-Bains, bringing together the leaders of Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, and the United States. Taiwan launches public program to recruit Chinese intelligence sources : Taiwan's National Security Bureau said on Sunday it is creating a secure online channel for Chinese nationals to covertly provide intelligence-related information, as officials in Taipei said an increasing number of people from China had recently approached Taiwanese authorities seeking ways to share intelligence information safely amid rising military tensions in the region. The bureau said the reporting system was modeled on practices used by U.S., British, and Israeli intelligence agencies, and comes as Beijing has ramped up its own online campaign aimed at identifying and punishing individuals it labels as supporters of Taiwanese independence. FIFA World Cup: FIFA reportedly the design Haiti submitted for its official 2026 World Cup jersey, on the grounds that it contained "political imagery." The jersey, designed by Colombian manufacturer Saeta, featured a patch that depicted a scene from the 1803 Battle of Vertieres, a decisive battle in Haiti's War of Independence from France. Haiti gained independence in 1804 becoming the world's first independent nation founded by formerly enslaved people after a successful slave revolt. Dear Friend,

C.S. Lewis is one of my favorite authors, full stop.

His writings were essential in deepening my faith in God and my understanding of the Bible. Maybe, since you opened my email, he has helped you, too.

Why are Lewis's words so powerful?

It's because he was a master at addressing life's most important questions. His vivid language is delightful and captivating to read.

Lewis's signature ability to communicate the truth about Christianity has inspired so many skeptics to **become** believers and even more Christians to renew and deepen their faith. He is certainly the greatest Christian apologist of the twentieth century.

To help you learn more about Lewis's works related to Christianity, we produced a powerful, free course, "**C.S. Lewis on Christianity** ," which you can now own on DVD absolutely free.

**Claim your FREE DVD set of "C.S. Lewis on Christianity" using this secure link:**

[https://info.hillsdale.edu/free-cs-lewis-christianity-dvd](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckc9q3DAQh59Gvtnojy3ZBx8SnIVA0lL20KPQSrI9IEtCIyf07cuGDfTc68ww33zz-_2u3w0EiNsPc_gZEHVBbTH4T0DMJa3pjA4iwrZX1Jxy2VLZskHnkjB7WzVv3DxwNq5j42emRjb0nFLR7LNk060feqWs4tNtoutqDFUTm1YhLbeigfm-kEo2MNkPrO_kMHJ1o6qX0zh5upKentmZ6rv7Cc6jTSnnFKCCxS6VrQnzXmtGIp4IvxB-gbimbocQ0JngO-9Owi9r8b612H5ZtXYvgBVMhPqndR-OiAtaIhZKORdPlFL2xqbl57K8XAmXZz00prNYT8TyLQ1xe7QO7-A8iFj8YSA8itYc2cAWiVgs6i-q_peq79THaIrVx0rE8vz6_Paif6n29Xptv__SlNnlTwgBUCrS0-1O6Ww6mvqfYX3M_G8AAAD__2qlpgE)

In this course, you will study Lewis's profound insights on the central topics of Christianity, including:
* Good and evil
* Conversion and faith
* Prayer and the Bible
* Suffering and death
* Heaven and Hell

The instructor, Michael Ward, is a distinguished visiting professor at Hillsdale College and a member of the Faculty of Theology and Religion at the University of Oxford. He wrote _Planet Narnia: The Seven Heavens in the Imagination of C.S. Lewis_ and _After Humanity: A Guide to C.S. Lewis 's The Abolition of Man_. He even spent three years living in Lewis's Oxford home as the resident Warden of The Kilns!

You'll find this course especially moving because it examines C.S. Lewis's beautiful writings about faith. You'll even trace Lewis's own journey from skeptic to believer. The combination provides an opportunity for you to grow in your knowledge and understanding of Christianity.

[So please join us in studying Christianity with C.S. Lewis and Michael Ward with this beautiful free DVD set.](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckc9q3DAQh59Gvtnojy3ZBx8SnIVA0lL20KPQSrI9IEtCIyf07cuGDfTc68ww33zz-_2u3w0EiNsPc_gZEHVBbTH4T0DMJa3pjA4iwrZX1Jxy2VLZskHnkjB7WzVv3DxwNq5j42emRjb0nFLR7LNk060feqWs4tNtoutqDFUTm1YhLbeigfm-kEo2MNkPrO_kMHJ1o6qX0zh5upKentmZ6rv7Cc6jTSnnFKCCxS6VrQnzXmtGIp4IvxB-gbimbocQ0JngO-9Owi9r8b612H5ZtXYvgBVMhPqndR-OiAtaIhZKORdPlFL2xqbl57K8XAmXZz00prNYT8TyLQ1xe7QO7-A8iFj8YSA8itYc2cAWiVgs6i-q_peq79THaIrVx0rE8vz6_Paif6n29Xptv__SlNnlTwgBUCrS0-1O6Ww6mvqfYX3M_G8AAAD__2qlpgE)

Warm regards,

Bill Gray '01
Vice President
Institutional Advancement

* * *
I wasn't going to write about last night's stupid UFC fight. I didn't want to give it any more oxygen. But having caught up on the clips, the corruption, and the sheer stupidity of it all, I can't let it go.
It would be easy to fixate on the most salacious parts. The offensive attack on Michelle Obama by one of these shameless, attention-seeking assholes. Trump paying the fighters in crypto. Eric Trump getting caught doing insider trading. The desecration of our sacred monuments. And so much more.
But I want to focus on a specific trend I'm noticing from the MAGA influencers being paid to pretend this was some undeniable act of patriotism -- when in reality it was a bunch of weird rich assholes circle-jerking and congratulating themselves on how cool they are, getting the "common folk" to fight for their entertainment.
Because last night was the perfect reminder of who these people really are and what drives them.
The modern Republican Party is fueled entirely by grievance. They do not care about anyone other than themselves. They have no ideas, no solutions, no ability to improve your life. They don't care about you. I'd go further: I think they hate you and I know they hate this country.
Most of the people in the MAGA movement, right up to Donald Trump himself, are driven by the perceived slights against them, because they are tiny special snowflakes who believe they deserve special treatment -- and they will now abuse the full power of the federal government to get it.
Here's the kind of thing I saw last night. MAGA influencers argued it was fine for Trump to throw this fight at the White House because Barack Obama once lit it up in pride colors -- as if those are remotely the same thing. They are so offended by the existence of gay people, so threatened by the idea that a symbol of love could fly over the people's house, that to them it justifies handing the entirety of Washington, D.C. over so Dana White and a pack of rich assholes can gamble and make more money at our house.
This pattern plays out over and over. They think it's fine for Trump to use the FCC to chase Jimmy Kimmel off the air, because Roseanne Barr got fired once for a vicious racist tweet about Valerie Jarrett. They think it's fine for Trump to steal billions and billions from the American taxpayer, because Hunter Biden misused his last name. They think it's fine to cover up the Epstein files and to treat women inside their own movement the way they do -- to abuse them physically and sexually -- because Bill Clinton lied about a blow job in the Oval Office decades ago.
They are furious about every perceived slight against them. And they are not angry about the things that should actually make them angry.
* * *

* * *
They should be angry that Elon Musk became the world's first trillionaire a few days ago--something he would never have been able to accomplish without American taxpayers footing the bill. They should be angry about an economy held hostage to the war in Iran, and the insane "peace deal" Trump rolled out at his birthday party like set dressing. They should be offended that the people's house got handed to Paramount and the UFC to turn a profit at your expense. They should be offended by the desecration of monuments that are supposed to mean something -- that are supposed to stand for the best of what this nation can become.
They would be angry about all of that if they cared about anything other than themselves. But grievance is profitable, and propaganda pays better than patriotism ever could.
This is a class of wealthy, powerful, well-connected people. They have everything they need. They have money. They have power. What they lack is everything that actually matters. No real community. No real love for one another. No depth. No originality. None of it. They are soulless assholes who never think about you and will never lift a finger to make your life better.
And that's the part that should worry all of us. Because what happened last night was another reminder that they no longer see any meaningful distinction between themselves and the institutions they control. The White House becomes a venue. The government becomes a weapon. The law becomes whatever is convenient at the moment. Once people convince themselves that power belongs to them by right, every norm, every guardrail, every democratic principle becomes expendable.
The damage from that mentality will not disappear overnight. It won't be undone by a single election or defeat at the polls. The corruption, the cynicism, the attacks on institutions, and the normalization of behavior that would have once shocked the conscience of the country are going to leave scars. Repairing them is going to take time.
But none of that means surrendering to it. It means recognizing what's happening clearly and refusing to accept it as normal. It means fighting for the institutions they are hollowing out, holding these people accountable wherever possible, and making sure they face consequences for what they've done.
That's why the only real answer to last night is not just outrage, but action at the ballot box -- a reckoning that begins in November. When the American people rise up, make their voices heard, and vote out as many of these assholes as we possibly can. Not because that alone fixes everything, but because it's the first step toward repairing what they've broken. Then the adults can take back over, and the long process of rebuilding can finally begin. This nightmare doesn't end the moment they lose power. But it doesn't end at all unless they do.

Grievance over governance. | | | Jun 15 | | | | | | | | | | | | I wasn't going to write about last night's stupid UFC fight. I didn't want to give it any more oxygen. But having caught up on the clips, the corruption, and the sheer stupidity of it all, I can't let it go. It would be easy to fixate on the most salacious parts. The offensive attack on Michelle Obama by one of these shameless, attention-seeking assholes. Trump paying the fighters in crypto. Eric Trump getting caught doing insider trading. The desecration of our sacred monuments. And so much more. But I want to focus on a specific trend I'm noticing from the MAGA influencers being paid to pretend this was some undeniable act of patriotism -- when in reality it was a bunch of weird rich assholes circle-jerking and congratulating themselves on how cool they are, getting the "common folk" to fight for their entertainment. Because last night was the perfect reminder of who these people really are and what drives them. The modern Republican Party is fueled entirely by grievance. They do not care about anyone other than themselves. They have no ideas, no solutions, no ability to improve your life. They don't care about you. I'd go further: I think they hate you and I know they hate this country. Most of the people in the MAGA movement, right up to Donald Trump himself, are driven by the perceived slights against them, because they are tiny special snowflakes who believe they deserve special treatment -- and they will now abuse the full power of the federal government to get it. Here's the kind of thing I saw last night. MAGA influencers argued it was fine for Trump to throw this fight at the White House because Barack Obama once lit it up in pride colors -- as if those are remotely the same thing. They are so offended by the existence of gay people, so threatened by the idea that a symbol of love could fly over the people's house, that to them it justifies handing the entirety of Washington, D.C. over so Dana White and a pack of rich assholes can gamble and make more money at our house. This pattern plays out over and over. They think it's fine for Trump to use the FCC to chase Jimmy Kimmel off the air, because Roseanne Barr got fired once for a vicious racist tweet about Valerie Jarrett. They think it's fine for Trump to steal billions and billions from the American taxpayer, because Hunter Biden misused his last name. They think it's fine to cover up the Epstein files and to treat women inside their own movement the way they do -- to abuse them physically and sexually -- because Bill Clinton lied about a blow job in the Oval Office decades ago. They are furious about every perceived slight against them. And they are not angry about the things that should actually make them angry. * They should be angry that Elon Musk became the world's first trillionaire a few days ago--something he would never have been able to accomplish without American taxpayers footing the bill. They should be angry about an economy held hostage to the war in Iran, and the insane "peace deal" Trump rolled out at his birthday party like set dressing. They should be offended that the people's house got handed to Paramount and the UFC to turn a profit at your expense. They should be offended by the desecration of monuments that are supposed to mean something -- that are supposed to stand for the best of what this nation can become. They would be angry about all of that if they cared about anything other than themselves. But grievance is profitable, and propaganda pays better than patriotism ever could. This is a class of wealthy, powerful, well-connected people. They have everything they need. They have money. They have power. What they lack is everything that actually matters. No real community. No real love for one another. No depth. No originality. None of it. They are soulless assholes who never think about you and will never lift a finger to make your life better. And that's the part that should worry all of us. Because what happened last night was another reminder that they no longer see any meaningful distinction between themselves and the institutions they control. The White House becomes a venue. The government becomes a weapon. The law becomes whatever is convenient at the moment. Once people convince themselves that power belongs to them by right, every norm, every guardrail, every democratic principle becomes expendable. The damage from that mentality will not disappear overnight. It won't be undone by a single election or defeat at the polls. The corruption, the cynicism, the attacks on institutions, and the normalization of behavior that would have once shocked the conscience of the country are going to leave scars. Repairing them is going to take time. But none of that means surrendering to it. It means recognizing what's happening clearly and refusing to accept it as normal. It means fighting for the institutions they are hollowing out, holding these people accountable wherever possible, and making sure they face consequences for what they've done. That's why the only real answer to last night is not just outrage, but action at the ballot box -- a reckoning that begins in November. When the American people rise up, make their voices heard, and vote out as many of these assholes as we possibly can. Not because that alone fixes everything, but because it's the first step toward repairing what they've broken. Then the adults can take back over, and the long process of rebuilding can finally begin. This nightmare doesn't end the moment they lose power. But it doesn't end at all unless they do. ## US, Iran Reach Deal to End War
The United States and Iran have [reached a peace deal](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2O6zAMBODT2J0CitaPU6h4Tbq8dkuDluiEC8UyZCVBbr_wXmFLgsAMvvm6TleSLOvtPz04tKVMK7_3zK1xnaTSujFFTkx5l_akJmWtpUwI6BQ4pe2USPJnMn0KCzPy0HPQftTWoAHT38M8O2Y_pPM8gjUaTFw4DfMCMNrZRt9LONLAaaudHVCfPDpHTicdHXiYsTPASVqpp-8ia7vzkj_lxfUUy6PP4d7atnfDvw4vHV5oOwDH6zhqk5i5w8tBUc9dvamqyLTzIpXV4VIMdGbDWltkGhNpYALnKGlvCAfqa0jbW3KW3fnOwO1Bkn-7258GewX8CQAA___K2H34) to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, Pakistan's prime minister announced Sunday. The signing is expected to take place on Friday in Switzerland. The agreement came hours after Israeli strikes near Beirut [nearly derailed](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAQRL_GZCC7sc1c4OASsrn0QtRAM_SusUd276D5-xX7C5tUUtIrvfp_n-7IkdPjHx4UZMtTorNGEqEyccH0JFxoJYyV5QuFcyo5T6DBt9q3xk0rcnxPtlnDRgTUNxTMcDPOgtW22YOzRs-ENDigecPlD87-5pzvb4MxjnTD4aJpb5zxrgfTDeA9erOaxetBz6CsppUll-4jc5KdtvjOLyrdko8mhl3kWVX_V8GoYDzPs1vSvFylgvFCKxj1FcYqGC-n9vJphUio1JZrQYptlcKfVNtIM6acul2O2JSwPk-OkasflNWPAzn-zMqvvnoF-A4AAP__yWd8hA) the deal, with President Trump bluntly criticizing Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and warning both sides to stand down. The deal creates a 60-day framework for broader talks on Iran's nuclear program and frozen assets, but does not resolve either issue. The U.S. will ease sanctions to allow Iran to [sell more of its oil](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGu4yAQheGnwZ0jZowhKSi2cZdtt7QmZgizwibCJFHe_sp5hVsf6Ze-8-86X0mybPe_tLJvscwbv_fMrXGdpdL2YFo4MOVd2pOalK2WMqNG22vbwzgHkvyZTRd8ZEYeOvbgzjAaNNp0yRuzkINL5BgoIgZHg7m5eAawFC6gO_FHTVsYwY4DwsmhtWQhwGK10zdURnOQVurpf5GtJY75U15cT0tZu-xTa49dDX8UTgqnljhJzsemcEpl5QOkcKKwyiZ7q1-Ewmm84DAC9M-9P6D9V9of1D7xreRMSeHUVR8eb8lZduuU0feV5Fvv2q_uenn8CQAA__9dRX6o) and strengthen its economy. Republican critics have already said the terms are [no better than the 2015 deal](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOpDAMgOGnCV1GiQlhKSiuodtrr0TexMz4NpOgxOyKe_oT8wrbuLH0y_7-vK_vyInz_Tc-aZatrJm-WyIRqitXzDthoEiYGsuBwiXXUlYw4LXx2g5rRE7n6ro4b0RAfUezHd_s4MAZ1z1mM27ThC5OFqwzYxz6aYiDC3Ga3sLm-o7nq2a8HawferC3EbxHb6MN3ozmA5QzFFlKvf0tnOVBWzrLF9VbKM8uzQ-Rvan-l4JFwZLPvTS5VgqWK6xgMdewTsFyNH39p2CRejx3HSoLB_5HTXOrSElvpeomlT8533WiD8wl64Zn0yiC4VOHcqSoIyU89QWkX0L6IlKwdHWO-zenxM2Pypn7Ezm9DpUf6X7N8D8AAP__oFWOdA) Trump pulled out of during his first term.
## Situation Room Might Have Been Recorded
White House officials believe two reporters [obtained audio recordings](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO2zAQRL-G6miQK4q6K1QYCdRd2pQCLS6tzVFcYUmf4L8PnAD5gdSDGcx7Pz-Wj0CZyv1H2HFqiZeCZ83YGspCEsqBYcWIIVdqj9CIizAvYMBr47UdlhgoPxfXxSkhAvYdTnZ8s4MDZ1y3TWBTwmCHN5PG3vne9H6072kEPwzRubWj6bVmvB2sH3qwlxG8D95Gu3ozmhsoZzBSY7n8Yiptw5Sf_IVyWXnv8rS1dlTVXxXMCubzPC97La9MwYxFP6qC-QWlYOa2oSiYmzz2QweKWHXCILrgqZ8sn7rRjlULHiwNpWq-tUAFo_6Hr4V514IrS6Ryrzrx3_6N-VPBHERfrzB8e9-_dzLF46ScqfpROXPfA-U_r9t_qf6a4HcAAAD__0HWlJI) of classified Situation Room meetings for a forthcoming book on the Trump presidency, an unprecedented breach of one of the most secure rooms on Earth. The book, _[Regime Change](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkMGqnDAUhp8m7pTkGI92kUUpCLOYUrrpUs6Yo54SE4npyPTpL3Nf4W7_H74Pvj_36U4SJK4_aWdXljRFvs7ApXCeJFM8mGb2TOGU8o-KpJhTmkAD1hpr002eJLwmW3m3MAO3FTvTD6azYLWtNqdN-63n3iyLNXrgbhgAsTW0oHmAIajEvWkaTWewa8E0PSASGm9m1L1-gLKavZSUm79JYtl4Ca_05NzMaa-C20o5TtV-VzAqGK_ramin_ym-bwXjb15l5_rHRnHl-hZP8Vzf9oOzUKh_ZX4PcX4pGP2hYDSIg8YeLFTZ-eOSEOTEXlm97iThU1q-VOrp4CMAAP__eah68g)_ , due out June 23, is based on roughly 1,000 interviews and includes verbatim dialogue from top-secret meetings about the Iran war and the Epstein files. Vice President JD Vance proposed enlisting Tucker Carlson to interview convicted sex trafficker Ghislaine Maxwell in prison to clear Trump's name, while Trump wanted the [Epstein issue buried entirely](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFutDAQhJ_GdEb2AuancHEN3f1KlZRogQU2Z2xk-w7d20fkFdKNNNKn-ebrPtyRHfv1P-5k8xIGT2dylDPFgSP6g3CimdAlzk_MHHwMYQAFRiojdTPMyO491MVsFyKgqiCr23-6qaFWdbFZQtWNldFdg2oCnLpZq5FINW29mI66gu1FU0Y32jQV6LIFY9DoWU9GtWoEUSuaOYdYfgf2eaPFvcOLYjmFvXB2y_lIoroJ6AX053mWe_JXJ6AnL59JQH9JCeiP4DjzdMVIK-8kpw39StLTKccQHjLS63KVOT73Q2bCXSZJR8rEXjrCh1wI4wXAKG83aB4f988i2vk42TlOphW1Wndk97su_-nSl4WfAAAA__890Yvl). The White House has not disputed the accuracy of the quoted conversations. Independent recording devices are forbidden in the Situation Room. Read about additional leaks [here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2OrDAQhE8DGch_GCZw8BKyeemGqIEGetVgZPcOmtuvmCts9kklleqrr-fwBGI61v-wY5AlDgdemVEE00AJjhNhwhmBM8kPCMUjxTgYZXylfKWbYQbi9-DKOSyIBm2JQbedbpxxypVbmGGcmlGNFhGXycM4-u5hvYPuYbsH2pLC3aa8brRvrNF1a7wHr2c9edWq0RRO4UwSU_0d6ZANF37HF6Z6invJYRM5c2H_FaYvTH9dV_2GLcY7LUx_6xSmPyOT0HQjJKGJ8camyidD3gizVAlfyB_DXO2wroTVBiOmHY5KO62s1srVm-xcpjCfFzFT9m3h1LoD8WeN_OnCVzC_AQAA__9oG4ap).
## UFC Fights Rock the White House
The White House hosted its [first professional sporting event](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2u2zAQhE8jdTTI5Y_sgkUadS9tSoESl9YGlCiQKyvv9oGdI6SdwQxmvl9f01egTPvzZ9jQcyrTjlfLyIx1ohr2A8OCEUNuxGdgKnstZQIJTkgnlJ1ioPw9mT76hAioe_RquCtrwEjTrx600Y-IbrYhRTsMYOSMKtkU8a5Bu578u006ZZWzGtRtAOeCU1EtTg5yhs5IjMSl3n4X2nnFlL_LC-ttKVuf_cp8tE7_6GDsYLyu67bPy_vF2-9gbEep3DoYN_qDUWyhMoUswj8x0wvFnMuzg_FMi0gVMZZNgJXiWolRrOVsKBI9VxZcz-0Qn8x5xMDYRF32oM3jcXd99fG4KGdqbuiMfG6B8mck_xfZl4e_AQAA__8ycY6b) Sunday night as UFC Freedom 250 turned the South Lawn into a fight arena for President Trump's 80th birthday. The crowd sang _Happy Birthday_ as Trump sat cageside next to promoter Dana White. Fighters walked through the Grand Foyer, Green Room, and Red Room on their way to the South Lawn, while the U.S. Marine Band played walk-out music and a B-1 bomber shook the ground with afterburners past midnight. Watch Trump and White [kick off the event from the Oval Office here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGu4yAQRb_G7ogAA84rKLZx97bd0hrDEM8Gg4XHsfL3q-wvvPpKV-ecP9_zN1Cm8vgNG3pOdS54HRmZsc3UoOwIASNCPohPYKql1TprqZ2QTig7R6D8nk0ffULUOPTo1XhX1mgjTb96DXKJcUk2KHOHrxiki8HgF6S4pAWgJ_95k05Z5eyg1W3UzoFTUQUnR7nozkiMxLXd_lYqvGLK7_rCdgt167NfmfejG351eur0dF3XrSzhY_HZOz29KGLt9MTt3HYBJYoIBcS1EqO4ID9FPVlwfSCv2ARX8aTwFDUlcaYgUkOMdRPaSqGdlffBOGWN6puP-0U50-HGzsjHBpT_I_GPOr68_hcAAP__kO2IGw). American underdog Justin Gaethje stunned the card by handing champion Spain's Ilia Topuria the first loss of his career, winning the lightweight title after Topuria's corner [stopped the fight](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuwyAQQL8Gb0RwBpwODF28pWtHi9iHuQobC86J8vdV-gudn_Se9L5v0y1Qpn39Cht6jmXa8dkyMmOdqIb9wDDjgiE34jMwlb2WMoECJ5WT2k5LoPyaTLf4iAjYd-j1cNXWgFGmSx6s7lGrEMPd9srMQ7wHq5x26Iw1MHfk3zbltNXO9qAvAzgXnF707NSg7iCMwoW41MtPoZ0TxvwqD6yXuWxd9on5aKL_FDAKGDlhopzfTMB4lEzzS8DYjlK5yTVstK8CRvsB6uqMPOMsY0VcyibBKvlMxChTORtKrud2CBi76pfjSTlTc4Mwat0C_QU6_texh4ffAAAA___fdn6W) following a bloody fourth round. Gaethje celebrated with a backflip off the cage and a handshake with the president. About [4,000 watched from the South Lawn](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGu3CAQRb8Gd6xgMHi3oIgUuXtRupQWhvF6ImwsGK-1fx9tfuHVV7o65_z5mr4CZdqfv8KGnpcy7Xi1jMxYJ6phPzBETBhyIz4DU9lrKRMocFI5qe2UAuX31HfJL4iApkOvh7u2PfSq71a_6BnT7OI86ME8HnfQNswWw5wAwiMOHfnPm3LaamcN6NsAzgWnk45ODWoG0StMxKXe_hbaecUlv8sL6y2Wrct-ZT6aMD8EjALGMMePwWcTMP4umZhiEzDS3iih5HpuR5PnEuVCz5XltRKjXMvZULZy8ipzuHYBY-NS38KMlIT5qY2564eztqs-HRflTM0NolfPLVD-T8Lfyvfy8C8AAP__4xiEfQ) while more than 100,000 fans packed the Ellipse across the street to watch on giant screens, making it one of the largest public gatherings in Washington in years.

name: Sara Jacobs
subject: I voted NO on the $1.142 trillion military bill
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Sara Jacobs for Congress
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=25 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=25]
Last week, I voted no on the $1.142 trillion National Defense Authorization Act in the House Armed Services Committee. I want to tell you exactly why.
First, a quick explainer: the NDAA is a yearly military authorization bill that sets our defense policies and funding limits for the year.
It's one of the most important bills Congress passes — an annual opportunity to address the needs of our service members and military families, and meet the national security challenges of the 21st century with real solutions.
I’m San Diego’s only member on the House Armed Services Committee, where I'm incredibly proud to represent the largest military community in the country. I hear firsthand from service members and military families about their struggles to make ends meet, find affordable housing, and access child care.
While millions of Americans are living paycheck to paycheck, struggling to afford gas and groceries each week, my Republican colleagues decided that what we really needed was a $1.142 trillion military budget. If we want to create meaningful and lasting security, it won’t come from building more ships and planes and enriching defense contractors – it’ll come from investing in the American people – something that we’ve failed to do.
On top of all that, Donald Trump has used the U.S. military as his own personal army to do his bidding. He’s illegally deployed troops in American cities, conducted strikes in Iran and off the coast of Venezuela without the constitutionally-required approval of Congress. He’s threatened to invade Greenland and Cuba. He’s even floated the idea of sending troops to polling locations.
This bill utterly fails to constrain the weaponization and politicization of our military by the Trump administration. Our armed forces are not a political tool — and any bill that doesn't put real guardrails around how this administration can use them is a bill I won't support.
I take what’s in this bill very seriously, which is why throughout this process, I fought for (and won) key provisions that would improve it:
* I secured provisions to expand access to IVF for military families and lower the cost of child care.
* I fought to get transparency on the U.S. strike on the girls’ elementary school in Minab, Iran, which killed more than 175 civilians, most of whom were young girls and teachers.
* And I secured provisions to ensure accountability on AI's use by the Pentagon.
I'm proud of that work. But those wins don't make up for a bill that leaves the door wide open for Trump to keep weaponizing our military for his own political ends.
I’ll continue pushing for the best possible version of this bill, but the best way to pass an NDAA we’re actually proud of is to flip the House in November. Doing that means real guardrails, real accountability, and real support for our service members and their families. That's what I'm fighting for.
I’ll proudly keep pushing on these issues from inside the Capitol, but I’m going to need your help if we want a shot at making real progress. Are you with me? If so, I hope you’ll sign your name and let me know that you’re all in to flip the House this November. [https://secure.ngpvan.com/g4DRL3dhMUWMyupqy_cVcg2]
ADD MY NAME [https://secure.ngpvan.com/g4DRL3dhMUWMyupqy_cVcg2]
And if you want to read the full POLITICO article, you can do that here [https://www.politico.com/live-updates/2026/06/03/congress/house-dem-proposes-bill-to-help-agencies-create-ai-rules-00947487] .
Thank you so much for reading and for your support.
–Sara

_Virginia Pride and Diversity Richmond at our inaugural parade_
Everyone deserves to live with dignity and without fear. That has always been the promise of our Commonwealth.

But we know that promise is under pressure. Across the country, LGBTQ+ Americans are facing a wave of attacks on their rights.

**Here in Virginia, we are holding the line.**

This November, Virginians will vote on a constitutional amendment to guarantee marriage equality for all. We will make it clear, in law and in practice, that every Virginian’s rights are protected.

I remain committed to ensuring that every Virginian feels welcome and safe in our Commonwealth. And during this month of celebration and resolve, I hope you will join me.

Happy Pride,

Governor Abigail Spanberger

# [Oil plunges below $80 as Trump completes Iran Hormuz deal](https://substack.com/redirect/19dd2f78-5868-40e1-ae52-4d6aff5b2ef6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
President Donald Trump **[announced a completed deal with Iran](https://substack.com/redirect/b23cf07e-1915-4b2c-a287-368421cec35a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to reopen the Strait of Hormuz without tolls and end the U.S. naval blockade, driving U.S. crude prices below $80 a barrel for the first time since March amid broad market relief.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/19dd2f78-5868-40e1-ae52-4d6aff5b2ef6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Crude futures tumble sharply:** U.S. crude dropped 5.64% to $79.99 per barrel while Brent fell 5.07 percent to $82.90 in early European trading on the news.
* **Trump signals rapid reopening:** The president posted that ships should start engines with the strait opening Friday after the Switzerland signing ceremony for mine removal purposes.
* **Pakistan confirms peace terms:** Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif stated the U.S. and Iran declared immediate permanent termination of military operations on all fronts including Lebanon.
* **Energy shares pressured lower:** Stoxx 600 energy sector fell 2.3 percent and FTSE energy dropped 4 percent with BP and Shell shares declining notably.

# [Hormuz traffic odds hit 58 % of normal by August on Kalshi](https://substack.com/redirect/19dd2f78-5868-40e1-ae52-4d6aff5b2ef6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Following President Trump's Iran deal announcement **[traders on Kalshi pushed odds of Strait of Hormuz traffic returning to normal](https://substack.com/redirect/e35d0f05-a431-4279-a4f7-680a3cd5ad07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** before August above 50% for the first time since late May with over 75% chance by year end.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/19dd2f78-5868-40e1-ae52-4d6aff5b2ef6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Odds surge after announcement:** Probability reached 58% for pre-August normalization and 75% before end of year after removal of U.S. naval blockade confirmed.
* **Trump clarifies timeline:** The strait opens after Friday Geneva signing for mine removal under Iranian arrangements with toll-free long-term access expected.
* **Qatar seeks more clarity:** Officials requested details on outstanding issues including freedom of navigation while Israel continues operations in security zones.
* **Vance notes early signs:** Vice President reported increased traffic flow in the past 24 hours as signing approaches.

# [Trump threatens 100% wine tariffs unless France scraps tech tax](https://substack.com/redirect/19dd2f78-5868-40e1-ae52-4d6aff5b2ef6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
President Donald Trump warned France it must eliminate its **[3% digital services tax on U.S. tech firms or face 100% tariffs](https://substack.com/redirect/49d01ecf-2c29-413d-8397-a16d4e439dad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on all champagne and wines exported to America ahead of the G7 summit.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/19dd2f78-5868-40e1-ae52-4d6aff5b2ef6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Macron directly addressed:** Trump said he asked the French president not to charge American companies otherwise imposing full tariffs on wines and champagnes.
* **Tax targets big tech:** The 2019 levy applies to gross revenues in France from large firms including Amazon Meta and Alphabet.
* **Wine exports significant:** U.S. market accounts for roughly one fifth of French wine sales valued at about $2 billion dollars annually.
* **Prior threats recalled:** Similar retaliatory moves occurred in 2019 and earlier this year including 200% tariff proposals on French wines.

* * *
* * *
# [SpaceX surges six percent after record IPO at $2 trillion valuation](https://substack.com/redirect/19dd2f78-5868-40e1-ae52-4d6aff5b2ef6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
SpaceX shares **[gained 6% on their first full trading day](https://substack.com/redirect/dbdc9954-ab6c-47f9-8ab9-7084f348d4ca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after Friday's historic 19% jump in the largest initial public offering ever pushing the company's market capitalization above $2 trillion dollars.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/19dd2f78-5868-40e1-ae52-4d6aff5b2ef6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Musk eyes trillion revenue:** Elon Musk posted the company might reach approximately $1 trillion dollars in 2030 revenue and exceed it in 2031 after $18.7 billion last year.
* **Analysts divided sharply:** CFRA started with sell rating and $115 dollar target citing ambitious growth while NewStreet gave $165 dollar bullish view over long horizon.
* **Capital spending spikes:** First quarter expenditures hit $10.1 billion dollars mostly directed toward artificial intelligence nearly double prior year.
* **Launch dominance highlighted:** Experts noted at least ten year lead with Starship enabling massive orbital payloads for Starlink and data centers.

# [Fox agrees to acquire Roku in twenty two billion dollar deal](https://substack.com/redirect/19dd2f78-5868-40e1-ae52-4d6aff5b2ef6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Fox Corp. announced a **[$22 billion dollar cash-and-stock acquisition of Roku](https://substack.com/redirect/61b1d1b0-5f8d-4914-a1bd-0678fdda7488?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/61b1d1b0-5f8d-4914-a1bd-0678fdda7488?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)combining its news sports Tubi streamer with Roku's devices and channel in a major media streaming consolidation expected to close first half of 2027.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/19dd2f78-5868-40e1-ae52-4d6aff5b2ef6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Deal structure detailed:** Roku shareholders receive $160 dollars per share with Fox funding cash via $12 billion loan and existing cash Roku owners get 27% of combined entity.
* **Murdoch calls defining:** Fox CEO described it as reorienting around live news sports and advertising with plans to keep Tubi and Roku Channel separate.
* **Roku platform strength:** CEO Anthony Wood noted reach to over one hundred million households globally and $145 billion hours annual engagement.
* **Synergies projected:** Approximately $400 million dollars in run-rate cost savings expected plus additional revenue upside from complementary services.

* * *
# [Anthropic meets Trump officials over Mythos AI model suspension](https://substack.com/redirect/19dd2f78-5868-40e1-ae52-4d6aff5b2ef6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Senior Anthropic executives convened with Trump administration officials in Washington Monday **[seeking to resolve a government directive suspending access](https://substack.com/redirect/d5140740-645d-4b48-b738-8a38bc7ed308?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to its new Fable 5 and Mythos 5 AI models for foreign nationals citing national security.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/19dd2f78-5868-40e1-ae52-4d6aff5b2ef6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

And despite his lengthy time in the Senate, and witnessing the chaos and destruction of the first Trump administration, Bennet is in the top nine – out of the 47 Senate Democrats — who have voted to confirm Trump’s appointees since the start of 2025. _Bennet is out of step with what Coloradans want and expect from our next governor._ **FACT: Billionaires aren’t steering our people-powered movement for Colorado — YOU are.** Unlike Bennet’s, this campaign isn’t backed by out-of-state billionaires. We aren’t relying on check after check from big corporations or dark money groups to power our campaign. Instead, I committed over a year ago to show up across all four corners of our state and listen to you so I can deliver — with you — on the change we need as your next governor. We’ve built this movement together. And with you on board, we can win this primary together, too. _First, though, I need to ask for your support:_ **[Corporations and special interests have taken a side in this primary — and it isn’t ours, because they know that as your next governor, I’ll continue to hold them accountable. That means we need to pull together and meet this month’s fundraising targets _without_ their help. body:
| | | Peter, Trump's second term has been a disaster for working people. Prices keep going up. Billionaires keep getting richer. Corporate CEOs, crypto grifters, and Big Tech executives are making out like bandits while families struggle to afford groceries, rent, healthcare, and electric bills. And far too many of our elected leaders are standing by and letting it happen. **That's why I’m proud to accept the Working Families Party endorsement as I run for Congress in Tennessee's 9th Congressional District.** I have already shown the country what it looks like to fight back. After a mass shooting devastated Nashville's Covenant School, I demanded action while Tennessee politicians offered excuses. For refusing to stay quiet, Republicans expelled me from the state legislature. But I didn’t back down, and voters sent me right back. That's the kind of leadership working people deserve. **[Will you split a contribution today between my campaign and the Working Families Party to ensure that Congress is filled with leaders who will fight for our communities?](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9XWmUFCGka7M26m5V0fiJl1NJVoxAPmx3rQSDYLTOushUhunzt2yMaLaTronNiDVi1TbxEogCNFXs_WKSpugXGUsGv-r6TkgLUHgo-XzP58wBm1j09x8mgSfwoIInW0Q9buClSRhfM9iH2boLCkriOrPLqDaj3QWp1MxrcDeJePnSJ1cQbl5k4M4t57mY8fr0QBmOo3LOdOjuGJcIMozpSR7v2l9SQHDBfyC1iK4aBz6UjGTWqonMS8WwC6ePG6iZPetFIW5phyPd0M10wdCutR-k3ojs2o7gc4Ay8BA9roN75mzJoSJFiTHFecqzJlDXivJFAgOC9EMDF_6U5_Fa_AqyvSvhvx2l7tvX-g7m7tXrSxP5jgX8b1Ec4KoaT1RVj7s5su2QC5RJxcqn--e2UE2l5JCkRABBwE_DfmObT3iCz_k-ZjIM_VR1J56tuM7RNGvu9cr4aodL8zzfTYB5oA/4ri/hrMb-FsPSz-BvcIEsJvRxA/h0/h001.9LK72Kj52BtEyskTcj0OVRwHhYTYD7R5QRj4J08MD4M)** **[Donate $10 »](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9XWmUFCGka7M26m5V0fiJl1NJVoxAPmx3rQSDYLTOushUhunzt2yMaLaTronNiDViZgCSe0jLDumEiX7KHttvSrxnph50DTpvfIXc80yXeKEGsfxsZAe44Ii7OZGYxiqF8usUSjiecS9StpvRxaoHugcxU1Rg3f4aHbpTbTBiuwsm37Rc0d92g6QEyHvlQU6VjCf5J2S6qfpAYINuOPtZ7jo_UdsvP7UGeQGpPOZzOCkiLS85qbp96wvfYcCAdKpBbA0zhU7cpwMvJDap0GefbcnDrRQlpvu4smHo518ESM-DdOficc7X0RJlu3wUssM4fq2S8ytaVyMGVbjt0jYAT2rPbc4yo9H4RG5VRVNgj6xgmH2AeUDWo7P1T7vMz2QUdHI5WByWMCEq9YYhqj1LOKRS0lXlLfqpWs7FE_3PYoARhlrRt7WYWv2zuvrathfbDfY0scKWZ0Q1D06ZYGJlQw/4ri/hrMb-FsPSz-BvcIEsJvRxA/h1/h001.874leGtV_WES58BPYjbwD-jPgXQIchRZzY4JagvqtVE)** This race is about more than one congressional seat. TN-09 has become a flashpoint in the national fight over voting rights and representation. After the Supreme Court’s decision in _Callais v. Louisiana_ , Tennessee became one of the first states to move forward with congressional maps that dismantled the state’s only majority-Black congressional district. Memphis was split into three separate districts, diluting the voting power of one of the South’s most important Black communities. The message was clear: some politicians would rather redraw the rules than compete for voters. Many people would look at a map like that and decide the race isn’t worth it. **But I’m not going down without a fight.** Because this fight has never been just about one election. It’s about whether working people and Black communities will have a voice in determining the future of our country. I have spent my time in office standing up to powerful interests that think they can buy our communities and dictate our future. I’ve fought corporate polluters, challenged unchecked corporate power, and stood with working families when others stayed silent. **That’s why I’m all in with the Working Families Party.** While others are willing to accept a future where powerful interests get to choose their voters, the Working Families Party is fighting back by organizing, building power, and electing leaders who refuse to back down. ******[Can you chip in to split a donation between my campaign and the Working Families Party? clean_body: | | | Peter, Trump's second term has been a disaster for working people. Prices keep going up. Billionaires keep getting richer. Corporate CEOs, crypto grifters, and Big Tech executives are making out like bandits while families struggle to afford groceries, rent, healthcare, and electric bills. And far too many of our elected leaders are standing by and letting it happen. That's why I’m proud to accept the Working Families Party endorsement as I run for Congress in Tennessee's 9th Congressional District. I have already shown the country what it looks like to fight back. After a mass shooting devastated Nashville's Covenant School, I demanded action while Tennessee politicians offered excuses. For refusing to stay quiet, Republicans expelled me from the state legislature. But I didn’t back down, and voters sent me right back. That's the kind of leadership working people deserve. This race is about more than one congressional seat. TN-09 has become a flashpoint in the national fight over voting rights and representation. After the Supreme Court’s decision in Callais v. Louisiana , Tennessee became one of the first states to move forward with congressional maps that dismantled the state’s only majority-Black congressional district. Memphis was split into three separate districts, diluting the voting power of one of the South’s most important Black communities. The message was clear: some politicians would rather redraw the rules than compete for voters. Many people would look at a map like that and decide the race isn’t worth it. But I’m not going down without a fight. Because this fight has never been just about one election. It’s about whether working people and Black communities will have a voice in determining the future of our country. I have spent my time in office standing up to powerful interests that think they can buy our communities and dictate our future. I’ve fought corporate polluters, challenged unchecked corporate power, and stood with working families when others stayed silent. That’s why I’m all in with the Working Families Party. While others are willing to accept a future where powerful interests get to choose their voters, the Working Families Party is fighting back by organizing, building power, and electing leaders who refuse to back down. **** Working people built this country. And together, we're building a future where our democracy belongs to all of us. In love and service, Rep. Justin J. Pearson Thoughts? Feedback? We want to hear it. Here's what's happening in Idaho.
And if you think it's just Idaho, you're not paying attention because this is playing out across the country.
Caldwell just rubber-stamped nearly 1,000 new homes on 280 acres near Lake Lowell. Three hundred apartments with retail mixed in.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/2060daab-0a77-4c23-b726-b1febd46a56b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
In Boise they're putting up a massive high-rise affordable housing facility so refugees and California's homeless population get a walkable neighborhood while the people who've been here for decades get to watch their property values and their community change overnight.
Or, what about this massive project south of Boise?
[](https://substack.com/redirect/23b36101-ea7c-4cf3-8004-49bc41400883?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
_**They needed cheap labor so they imported a new population. That 's the whole story.**_
But here's where it gets really ugly. Your tax dollars are funding relocation through NGOs that nobody audits. Just a few months ago I pushed a bill to force transparency on where that money goes and audit the orgs who do this. And Idaho legislative leadership (R) killed it. They looked at a bill that just said "show us the receipts" and buried it.
**Ask yourself why a Republican leadership team would fight to keep NGO funding in the dark. Who benefits from that?**
You know what happened to Virginia?
It was solid red for years before the developments went in, the demographics shifted, and fifteen years later it's deep blue. Conservatives there still walk around confused about it (like it's some mystery nobody could've predicted). Every person with a calculator saw it coming and nobody in leadership cared because the construction money was too good.
Many Idaho Republicans are running the same play right now by partnering with Democrats on "affordable housing bills" that let developers flood the state (while Idaho families who can't get into a home are left holding the bag).
And the people moving in?
Well... they hate you.
_**They 're never pulling the lever for your values. **_
_**They don 't even like you. **_
That's just the math of importing an electorate that has zero connection to what Idaho was built on. Assimilation isn't what happens. What happens is the voter rolls change and suddenly your state doesn't belong to you anymore.
Calvin Coolidge [saw all of this](https://substack.com/redirect/6b792b32-7156-494e-b953-f2e573bae386?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a hundred years ago:
> **" We want no such additions to our population as those who prey upon our institutions or our property." **
Prey upon. He called it what it was.
And then he went further:
> **" The retroactive immigrant is a danger in our midst. His discontent gives him no time to seize a healthy opportunity to improve himself. His purpose is to tear down. There is no room for him here." **
A sitting Vice President published that in a national magazine and nobody flinched because everyone understood it was just the truth. Now you say that in Boise and your own Republican leadership acts like you're the problem.
Coolidge's solution?
> **" He needs to be deported, not as a substitute for, but as a part of his punishment." **
Meanwhile Idaho Republicans can't even pass a simple audit bill for the NGOs relocating these people into your neighborhoods.
This is happening all over the country.
Virginia already fell. So did Colorado. Conservative voters had zero clue what they were signing off on. Your own guys sold you out and called it "economic development." By the time the voter rolls shift in Idaho (and they will), the Republicans who made it happen will be retired somewhere cashing consulting checks from the companies that paid for all of it.
_**Your own party needs to stop telling you that demographic replacement is economic growth (because you know it isn 't and so do they).**_
Wake up, Idaho.
And then do something about it.
**P.S.**[Here's how it happens in Idaho](https://substack.com/redirect/042225ef-9a21-4c9e-ac64-85ea7fb29a04?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) >>

I'm going to be brutally honest with you:
**If we lose here in Michigan, Democrats lose our shot to flip the Senate.**
But if we win, Democrats can take control of the Senate. And we can finally put a real check on Donald Trump's chaos agenda.
That's how high the stakes are in this race.
That's why I'm going to do something a little different in this Substack today: [I'm going to ask you to contribute to my campaign to help me keep Michigan blue.](https://substack.com/redirect/f1f9e64d-814a-4ece-98e3-d30723b1329a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
But I also want to say this: I know many of you are informed, engaged people who are on plenty of political lists, and I'm sure you get asked for money all the time.
So I don't ask lightly. And I want to tell you what your support actually means.
Yes, your contribution helps pay for the organizing, the voter outreach, the ads, and all the daily costs that go into winning a battleground race like this.
But it also says something about you.
It says you believe voters, not MAGA billionaires and out-of-state megadonors, should decide our elections.
It says you believe working families deserve leaders who will fight for them - and a government that makes life better, not harder.
It says you believe Michigan deserves a senator who loves this state. Someone who shows up, listens, and delivers. Not one who rubber-stamps whatever nonsense Donald Trump cooks up.
Yes, a $20 contribution helps power this campaign. But when I see it, I hear something more.
I hear: **I still believe this country can do better.**
I hear: **I 'm not giving up on Michigan.**
I hear: **We must flip the Senate.**
The polls keep showing the same thing: I'm the strongest Democrat in this race, and I can beat MAGA Mike Rogers in November. Independent voters are with us. The path is there.
But we still have to do the work - showing up every day, meeting Michiganders in every corner of this state, and building the kind of campaign that can win.
That is what your support makes possible.
Here is my ask: If you're in a position to chip in today, I'd be deeply grateful. [Will you give $20 or whatever you can afford?](https://substack.com/redirect/f1f9e64d-814a-4ece-98e3-d30723b1329a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/af792e27-96b2-4b9b-a06e-ae6cd8afc4ef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I'm grateful you believe in this fight. I'm grateful you believe in this state. I'm grateful for your help in keeping Michigan blue.
Together, we'll win.
More soon.
With grit and gratitude,
Haley
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/af792e27-96b2-4b9b-a06e-ae6cd8afc4ef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?

Straight from Democracy Docket, Team:
" President Donald Trump and the GOP are falsely claiming fraud over mail ballots in California’s primary . The lies are aimed at setting the stage to undermine this fall’s crucial midterms, when control of the House could hinge on the Golden State. "
Or take it from David Becker, executive director of the Center for Election Innovation & Research:
“ This is not about how fast California counts ballots ,” Becker said. “ All that [Trump] cares about is whether he wins or loses. And if he loses, he’ll create a fiction in his head to tell him otherwise .”
This is all a preview of what's to come in November, and it shows us how critical our work to protect mail-in ballots and inform voters is.

The lies went into overdrive as the counting of California's mail ballots caused a progressive Democrat to overtake Republican former reality TV star Spencer Pratt to make the November runoff race for Los Angeles mayor.
“ The Dumocrats, right before our very eyes, are stealing the Vote ,” Trump posted in response on social media. Vice President JD Vance, House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.), and numerous other GOP leaders have likewise raised suspicion about the count without any proof of wrongdoing or concrete examples of problems.
This won't just bring up problems with the mail-in ballots themselves, but could also lead to a flood of post-election litigation, as opponents of voting rights, alleging fraud or the potential for it, pull out the stops to get votes thrown out and to contest results.
We have to step up and stop this election denialism and subversion before it gains a foothold. Our fundamental right to vote depends on it.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]
