He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | In 1934, the government executed a legal maneuver that transferred billions in wealth overnight. name: Betty Gonzalez, Voto Latino
subject: When we participate at full strength, we can change election outcomes.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Voto Latino
body:
This is promising, but there’s still a ton of work to do.
#
Hi Peter, Betty here. Voto Latino’s Vice President of Digital Engagement.
I want to talk about the moment we’re in right now, but before I do: [**will you make a donation of $3 to Voto Latino before our mid-month fundraising deadline tonight at midnight?**](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260615-1-ak.hdMB8u&amount=3&refcode=em20260615-256&t=1&akid=256%2E1366028%2EN1VSqV)
Right now, _millions_ of eligible Latino voters are still unregistered, even though upcoming elections in key states could be decided by razor-thin margins.
A recent Unidos survey reveals something promising —**76% of Latinos plan to show up to the polls in November.** This is great, but this also means that 24% of Latinos are either not registered or unmotivated to show up.
That’s the gap we’re trying to fill. Our organizing is focused on finding those unregistered voters, helping them register, and turning them out — **because when Latino voters participate at full strength, we can change election outcomes.**
Republicans know that too. That’s why they’re pushing voter suppression laws and attacks meant to discourage our communities from participating.
Our path to building a movement they can’t ignore is simple.**Register more Latino voters, mobilize them, and show up at the ballot box. But we can’t do that without resources.**
Which is why we need support now more than ever. **We set a mid-month goal of raising $15,000 by tonight at midnight so we can continue to do this important work.**
**[If you can, please donate $3 or any amount now to help us reach our fundraising goal and keep registering, organizing, and mobilizing voters in the places that will decide what happens next.](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260615-1-ak.hdMB8u&amount=3&refcode=em20260615-256&t=2&akid=256%2E1366028%2EN1VSqV)**

Thank you,
Betty Gonzalez

No, seriously. Just $3.

They know this is one of the most competitive seats in the country – that’s why national election analysts just moved this race to "Toss-up."
They also know control of the House hinges on the outcome of our race.
That’s why the GOP is preparing to spend millions on this race.
But here's the thing: I've never had billionaire donors or Washington insiders powering my campaigns. I’ve had families, workers, and small business owners – folks who just want to believe in a better future.
I’m backed by working people chipping in what they can because they want someone in Congress who understands the challenges they're facing.
That's why your $3 matters.
* $3 helps us organize communities across Southwest Washington.
* $3 helps us reach independent and working-class voters who decide elections here.
* $3 helps us fight back against the flood of outside spending and attack ads that are already on the way.
And if enough people step up, even with just a few dollars, we'll have what it takes to win one of the closest races in the country.

After that, I went on to earn master’s degrees from MIT and Harvard. I served for 16 years as an active duty Army officer, deploying overseas six times to keep America safe and hunt down the world’s most dangerous terrorists. [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqiBIysd_1t7dQL51NYrcyKWf40KHRXV9g3KYxAlX2BXnPLyCycOEYkHBIYk09UAP4JIqlpqOdPiUQm6dADdQLvbm0OI3aLHjQ2AMbYjTnktZwEdi4anqPfmHrMohvO_D05s7LYN0At1-5JPfL3ijCMmlr2Zu9bnIiWKfOHvM0ZklxEH1SZk3QH8rfRnVaC3hZlca9wFwJws4YwSLc7hpZWSsA4KYgu5Z5nRSgEhHXQurfXE-ltoj8_Nq5RU9oike_wZhfbpHyfokOzdyzi_BbrOr6F_YlRfHzGIjssATBkA/4ri/l46GIlJZSjKTDMLLDRgwgg/h3/h001.44Txd7ualIpTG2hO21BJ-liKwVirTgQ8wY4QxYqrsTI) My entire career has been spent protecting Americans. But now, career politicians like Mike Lawler are throwing that away – and ripping health care and SNAP from millions, driving up costs, and threatening Social Security. **That’s why I’m running for Congress. Because I won’t tolerate what’s happening to our country.** And with our primary election coming up in just over a week, I’m counting on your support right now. When I was growing up, our South Carolina leaders were focused on attracting growth. Today, the challenge is different.

We're growing rapidly (too rapidly in some places) and that means every elected official has a responsibility to protect the
culture and quality of life that made people want to move here in the first place.

I grew up here. I understand this community because it's my community.

Too many politicians seem determined to turn South Carolina into the places people are leaving behind. We don't need Chicago
values. We don't need Los Angeles values. And we certainly don't need Washington telling us how to live.

The people moving here didn't come because they wanted more of what they left. They came because South Carolina is different.

I'm a product of South Carolina values, and I'm running for Congress to make sure those values are protected... not replaced.

Because of that commitment, I am honored to have earned President Trump's support.

I'm ready to get to work in Congress to deliver results!

Standing With You,

Wes Climer

[] [] Donate [] | Facebook [] | X / Twitter [] Donate [] Facebook [] X/Twitter [] [] When I was growing up, our South Carolina leaders were focused on attracting growth. Today, the challenge is different. We're growing rapidly (too rapidly in some places) and that means every elected official has a responsibility to protect the culture and quality of life that made people want to move here in the first place. I grew up here. I understand this community because it's my community. Too many politicians seem determined to turn South Carolina into the places people are leaving behind. We don't need Chicago values. We don't need Los Angeles values. And we certainly don't need Washington telling us how to live. The people moving here didn't come because they wanted more of what they left. They came because South Carolina is different. I'm a product of South Carolina values, and I'm running for Congress to make sure those values are protected... not replaced. These boxes aren't sitting around waiting for someone to need them.

They're already claimed. And we don't have extras.

By the time one batch goes out, more requests come in.

Different schools, different students, same situation -- they want to start something, and they're asking us to help them do it.

That's where things stand right now.

We have more students stepping up than we can fully support at the moment.

And I don't say that lightly.

Because for years, the challenge wasn't getting students the tools -- it was getting them to speak up at all. Most kept their heads down.

The Left has spent years trying to convince this generation to sit down, stay quiet, and be ashamed of their country and everything that makes it great.

And for a long time, it worked. But that's all changing.

We're not lacking interest or momentum. We're working to keep up with both. So here 's how you can help... Right now, there are students ready to step up -- they just need the tools to do it. An activism kit puts everything they need directly into their hands: ✅ Constitutions. ✅ Chapter guides. ✅ Flags. ✅ Materials to organize and lead. # The wind is at our back
---
| |
## _And we’re not stopping now_
---
| | **Peter,****We just had one of our most impactful weeks of the campaign so far. Thank you so much to everyone who came out to support Elizabeth by joining candidate forums & party meetings, knocked doors, and made phone calls. You are all the lifeblood of this campaign.**
**Early voting begins this week, and we’re approaching the final month of the primary campaign. But we can’t stop now. There’s too much at stake—both here in Virginia’s 1st District and across the country. The future of our democracy depends on flipping this seat and taking back the House. And we can’t do it without you.**
**We have another exciting week of events coming up. Elizabeth is participating in multiple candidate forums:**[**Tuesday, June 16th, at 5:30pm in Mechanicsville**](https://us.list-manage.com/qrMg1z6q43Q?e=2f83c585b2&c2id=3b13c473c2db4883f0cc0c9f59510326)**and**[**Wednesday, June 17th, at 6:00pm in Midlothian**](https://us.list-manage.com/Z2KG9OiOLU8?e=2f83c585b2&c2id=3b13c473c2db4883f0cc0c9f59510326)**.**
**On Thursday, we are hosting a**[**Day of Action in Henrico**](https://us.list-manage.com/3i5G8JSCcsa?e=2f83c585b2&c2id=3b13c473c2db4883f0cc0c9f59510326)**, which will feature a postcard writing session from 2-4pm and participation in the Henrico Dems Summer Social from 6-7:30pm. ****
On Saturday, June 20th, our campaign will be hosting an**[**ice cream social from 1pm-2pm in Gloucester**](https://us.list-manage.com/1BaNbkvHmlc?e=2f83c585b2&c2id=3b13c473c2db4883f0cc0c9f59510326)**. This event will serve as a moment to take a break from the chaos of campaigning and allow volunteers to connect with campaign staff and each other. Come join us for a sweet treat in the sun!**

name: Kimberly Bretches
subject: They’re trying to throw my husband in prison for protecting the community
body:
|
---
[ ](http://links.stoppingsocialistdems.com/u/click?_t=4dcc2aab65fd4d0da6a107b0eef86d43&_m=a4331be4ee864c0e95e6a6a0c8547234&_e=h3s6QNHq0xbSYFJUWzBEtwewAyhT9lvFBKtuWCecKQxRxeNZiYnY87JK-pLPTEEaxpBcvoTEN9O2Vb-h7XyjsHdoyuceRgGqxVy4ua54Pv1vBMWhz9j5HWBIspPaSt4ilc7r8coTXhfVAkaTLrWFXb5hNdi4-7Caliah4z4ITGrJurScI59lbkz0dGXq3xNgpy4b9IK1Go9vjz-sEfu8VvAyLCHQo5mpgREVA2_td19PA0tX9bWfoJcgt1Jv7T6HUBL6cpjpy8v22aTSEyMVMRQyoPa-czRqKogzRycSycUXl1YMWeIhQ2s9LlpbIsQutiVGfrIg3DmU7fSWE6t-iI5KhfGx6gTJgzyVu2CIpoWxEh5EivmNZhSSncCzQ0k2qLIH5Ja_rnpOptRC2VRLd8QV5r9Hlj0ckgFTY9ISxkuMyQn1FQ0Sqdux5aIfvo92) Officer Chance Bretches and his family — Austin, Texas
* * *
Dear Friend, My name is Kimberly Bretches. I'm a wife and a mother of four young children. And I'm writing to you today because I am out of options and I am terrified. I'll be honest, asking strangers for help doesn't come naturally to me. But neither does the idea of my husband spending the rest of his life in prison for doing his job — so here I am. Chance is a police officer in Austin, Texas. He is, without question, the best man I know. He has spent his career keeping dangerous people off the streets, protecting a city that doesn't always make it easy to do so, and coming home every night to a family that needs him. His supervisors have praised him for his professionalism, for his instincts, for his dedication. He is exactly the kind of officer you want showing up when things go wrong. | By every measure, Chance did everything right. He used department-approved tools, following his training, to protect his fellow officers and the people of Austin.
---
And in May of 2020, things went very wrong in Austin. For three consecutive days, our city was under siege. Violent agitators hurled rocks, frozen water bottles, and exploding fireworks directly at police officers. Buildings were vandalized and looted. Police vehicles were set on fire. A rioter was caught with a Molotov cocktail. Officers were injured. The city was teetering on the edge of complete chaos, and everyone knew it.
On May 31st, the third day, when the mob was larger and more dangerous than it had ever been, Chance was on the front lines. He did what he was trained to do. He deployed non-lethal, department-approved beanbag projectiles to stop the aggression and protect his fellow officers and the people of Austin. The crowd eventually dispersed. The city held.
**No one questioned what he did that night. His supervisors praised his response. His department stood behind him.**
And then Austin elected District Attorney José Garza.
Instead of holding the rioters accountable — the ones who threw the fireworks, who lit the fires, who carried the Molotov cocktails — Garza turned his attention to the officers who stopped them. He launched an indiscriminate campaign against law enforcement, using the power of his office not to protect the public, but to make political examples out of good cops.
Chance became one of his targets.
| Chance now faces up to 99 Years in prison — for following his training.
---
My husband now faces up to 99 years in prison. Not because he did anything wrong. Not because his department found fault with his actions. Not because any credible review of that night concluded he acted improperly. But because one politically-motivated prosecutor decided the officers who held the line deserved to be punished for holding it. This case has been grinding through the system for years now. The trial has already been delayed several times and is **now scheduled for June of this year.** Every continuance, every filing, every hearing means more hours of legal work, and more bills our family has to find a way to pay. I am asking for your help because we cannot do this alone. The National Center for Police Defense has been in Chance's corner, and your donation goes toward funding his legal defense, ensuring he has the representation he deserves as he walks into that courtroom in June.

If you believe that the men and women who run toward danger deserve better than this, [please give today](http://links.stoppingsocialistdems.com/u/click?_t=4dcc2aab65fd4d0da6a107b0eef86d43&_m=a4331be4ee864c0e95e6a6a0c8547234&_e=h3s6QNHq0xbSYFJUWzBEtwewAyhT9lvFBKtuWCecKQxRxeNZiYnY87JK-pLPTEEaxpBcvoTEN9O2Vb-h7XyjsHdoyuceRgGqxVy4ua54Pv2Bn2cKd_4MIxAVX0fDpg_urB3TgtFqT1aUgBrDqyrS5-C8BAM21g49qFVM-O8uFYyvP3-0oLzEY2oiJ_POn0pa0ufQG6m1LNFZeYpi84lPXQWhw17MkhvOfcX_u-06bMZ3e5tGpr6dx0q9Qu_3A5f_pQWMSV8GpPVVVv3R9T9Ug38Oa1z6iAqAAWgoKHN8BD4n2hDTFPmHgO0FvSNl0dP4QPf5pxU0NbhAonvzrTjix6fBIGsW5-vlIUYdJZkYZpme4LdR0W03FUbZcImqAX6KXbygmS3Oyhrig960D_qaC__jMQtnYWgSQt7bYhpK7T5KjyaHxNSW_MepUCeZ6Yi5). Every continuance, every filing, every hearing means more hours of legal work, and more bills our family has to find a way to pay. I am asking for your help because we cannot do this alone. The National Center for Police Defense has been in Chance's corner, and your donation goes toward funding his legal defense, ensuring he has the representation he deserves as he walks into that courtroom in June. | · · · or any amount you can give If you believe that the men and women who run toward danger deserve better than this, . Whatever you can. No amount is too small, and our family will not forget it. Chance stood between Austin and chaos on May 31st, 2020. He didn't hesitate. He didn't run. He did his job. Now I'm asking you to stand with him. With gratitude and hope, Kimberly Bretches Wife of Officer Chance Bretches, Austin Police Department | P.S. Chance's trial is this June. We are closer than we've ever been to getting Chance in front of a jury that will hear the truth, but we need the resources to get there. ** National Center for Police Defense · Defenders for Justice

clean_body: We're ready. Our candidates are ready. | = Peter, I want to talk about something I look at every single day: our electoral map. After the latest round of redistricting, there are now 14 more congressional districts across the country where Donald Trump got 55% of the vote or more. Let that sink in for a second. 14 more districts that are, on paper, deeply hostile turf for any Democrat. Why am I telling you this? Because I think you deserve the honest picture. And because I want you to understand exactly what EMILYs List is up against as we fight to take back power. = | = The GOP spent years engineering this advantage — and they're counting on us to be demoralized by it. But that's not how EMILYs List operates. When the landscape shifts, we shift with it. When the map gets harder, we get smarter. That's what we've done for decades, and it's how we're approaching this cycle, too. EMILYs List has a proven track record of taking on tough fights and electing Democratic women across districts many people would consider "tough terrain." Those wins didn't happen by accident. We recruited. We did the homework. We found Democratic pro-choice women who are the right fit for their communities — women who understand the voters in their communities, who know what's at stake, and who make the case in the places where it matters the most. That's the EMILYs List difference. It's about finding the right woman for the right race, and then making sure she has everything she needs to win. And after decades of doing this work, we know one thing for sure: Maps don't vote. People do. When you put the right candidate in front of the right voters — and give her the tools to make her case — tough races become winnable races. We're ready. Our candidates are ready. | Today, the establishment tried to silence us.
Just hours before our rally was set to begin, our venue canceled on us with no notice. It was the third venue this week to back out of an event with our campaign.
I won't lie - it was crushing. Our team and organizers had spent days preparing, and suddenly we were scrambling at the last minute, worried the whole event might collapse. So, we decided to take to the Capitol to protest against this blatant attempt to silence us - but we had no idea if folks would follow.
But on four hours' notice, Denver came with us.
Neighbors rearranged their day and folks showed up in full force because they know the freedom to gather, speak, and demand better cannot depend on whether the political establishment approves of your message.
That is the heart of this campaign.
When you challenge big money in politics, when you say health care should be guaranteed, when you call for an end to the genocide in Gaza, when you fight to abolish ICE, and when you insist that our democracy belongs to the many and not the wealthy few - the people who benefit from the way things are do not answer with a better argument.
They try to make you smaller - but we refuse to shrink.
While my opponent, Diana DeGette, who has held this seat for 30 years and taken millions in corporate pac donations, launches a new round of disgusting attacks against my character, leans on dark money, and signals once again for super PACs to rescue her campaign, I'm staying focused on working people.

I am proud to have won one of the most competitive House races in 2022. My race led the way for a new generation of leadership in New York.

New Yorkers told the Democrat establishment that they were tired of their failed leadership, which had done nothing to improve their lives.

New Yorkers told the Democrat establishment that they were tired of their failed leadership, which had done nothing to improve their lives. Ever since I was elected, I’ve worked hard in Congress to make real progress on lowering costs, strengthening public safety, and delivering results for working families. I am constantly battling the radical Left, who have taken hold of New York City and are fighting for socialist policies. Peter, I know how detrimental these policies can be, and I need Jackie Mary Auringer fighting alongside me in Congress to ensure extreme policies from Mamdani don’t infiltrate the Hudson Valley. Jackie was born and raised in the Hudson Valley and understands the real issues facing many families in her community. Jackie is a hard worker who will not back down from delivering real results for New York’s 18th district. I am glad to support her race for Congress and know we could use more young conservative leaders in Congress who are not beholden to special interests. In order to protect our conservative House majority and build on our momentum of fighting for affordability and lowering taxes for New York families, Jackie’s opponent is well-funded and has wealthy liberal donors bankrolling his campaign. Just like in my race, Jackie is supported by grassroots New Yorkers who love our state and country. Peter, it’s folks like you who stepped up in my race and made all the difference. Now, I’m asking you to step up for Jackie. She can win this. But not without you. Jackie and I are counting on you. body:
Will you support my friend Gina?
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260615_2_wendy.b57RB2&refcode=em20260615-1344&amount=5&t=1&akid=1344%2E299639%2EZL4c7p)
Hi Peter, it’s Wendy Davis.
Let me tell you a bit about why Gina’s campaign is so important to me.
But before I do, [**will you please make a $5 contribution to my friend Gina’s campaign?**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260615_2_wendy.b57RB2&refcode=em20260615-1344&amount=5&t=2&akid=1344%2E299639%2EZL4c7p)
I grew up in Texas. I’ve raised my children, built a career, and made a life here.
Early on, I learned that Texas was special. That no matter where you started, you had a chance — that hard work and determination could carry you forward. That belief is what has shaped my life and everything I’ve fought for in public service.
**I’m proud to be a Texan** — but to be honest, the state I love has become harder to recognize after more than a decade of Governor Abbott’s disastrous leadership.
Communities are being left behind because Abbott is doing the bidding of his billionaire donors, rather than working to improve the lives and the opportunities of the people he was elected to serve.
Not only does Texas deserve better, but we also can do better. We can elect Gina this year. And I know it’s possible because she’s already within 3 points of Abbott in the polls — far closer than either I or Beto ever came.
**I know Gina. I’ve watched her lead._And I’ve seen exactly what she’s made of._**
When her community’s schools were threatened, she didn’t wait — she stepped up and fought back to keep schools open. When Abbott pushed the agenda of the big corporations, she stood her ground and beat him again and again. And Peter, that kind of leadership really matters.
Gina is the person we want leading Texas. And together, we can make it happen.
Gina doesn’t need to match Abbott’s $106 million war chest to win — but she does need all of us standing with her and giving this everything we’ve got.
**[If you’re ready to defeat Abbott and chart a brighter future for Texas, pitch in $5 or whatever makes sense for you.](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260615_2_wendy.b57RB2&refcode=em20260615-1344&amount=5&t=3&akid=1344%2E299639%2EZL4c7p)**

Much love,
— Wendy

subject: Our Community’s Role in Protecting America’s Edge in Space
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Vince Fong for Congress
body:
Space has become one of the most important arenas for national security, economic growth, and technological innovation in the 21st century. | | |
---
| |
# Our Community’s Role in Protecting America’s Edge in Space
---
| Dear Friend, Space has become one of the most important arenas for national security, economic growth, and technological innovation in the 21st century. As other nations, especially China, continue to try to expand their capabilities in space exploration, satellite deployment, and related defense technologies, the United States faces growing pressure to maintain its leadership position. Recently, I introduced H.R. 8198 the Outpace in Space Act, legislation focused on strengthening America’s competitiveness in space. The proposal is part of a broader effort in Congress about how to ensure the United States remains at the forefront of innovation, security, and scientific advancement in orbit and beyond.
* Strengthening America’s Space Industrial Base — Supporting domestic innovation, manufacturing capacity, and advanced aerospace technologies critical to U.S. competitiveness.
* Enhancing National Security Coordination — Improving coordination between federal agencies and strategic partners involved in space and defense operations.
* Supporting Research and Development — Encouraging continued investment in next-generation technologies, satellite systems, and emerging aerospace capabilities.
* Promoting American Leadership in Space — Reinforcing the United States’ position as the global leader in commercial, civil, and national security space activities.
* Reducing Reliance on Foreign Adversaries — Addressing vulnerabilities tied to foreign supply chains and strategic competitors in critical space technologies.

The legendary Chuck Yeager broke the sound barrier in our backyard. Our community is continuing to develop the advancements in aerospace and defense technology that not only create jobs but defends America. This legislation is an ongoing effort in Congress to best to position the United States in an increasingly competitive global space environment. As this discussion continues, we will keep you updated on developments. Thank you for staying informed. Sincerely, Vince Fong

subject: Fresh from the Trail: This week's campaign update!

body:
High-fives in Rosalia, Mule Days in Reardan, Lind Combines, and Fairfield Flag Day!

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/NwXrUW_5KWu?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238)
|
---
| |
# Lind Combine Demolition Derby and Parade
---
| | _Click on the picture below for a video of Team Baumgartner at Lind Parade!_
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/jf5TWUWWWDi?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238)
| | This past weekend, Team Baumgartner proudly rolled into Lind for the annual Combine Demolition Derby and community parade. My team had a great time marching in the parade, waving to the enthusiastic crowds, and celebrating the agricultural spirit that brings our community together.
Even more exciting, we were thrilled to sponsor two powerful combines competing in the derby. We cheered them on as they battled it out for victory! A huge thank you to everyone who came out to support the event. Events like these highlight the hard work and camaraderie of our farming community, and we’re grateful to be a part of it!
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| |
---
|
---
| |
# The Red, White, and Blue: Fairfield Flag Day Parade
---
|
---
| | Team Baumgartner also marched in the Fairfield Flag Day Parade this past weekend. We proudly walked the route carrying our signs and handing out candy through the streets lined with cheering families. It was a wonderful opportunity to celebrate the red, white, and blue alongside our neighbors, honoring the freedoms and values that make our country so strong.
The day was filled with patriotism, smiles, and a great sense of community pride. We loved being a part of this special tradition and want to thank the Fairfield organizers and everyone who came out to make the event so memorable!
---
|
---
|
---
| |
# High-Fives and Hometown Spirit at Rosalia Battle Days!
---
| | I loved being out at Rosalia Battle Days with my wife Eleanor, our kids, and great volunteers. Some members of the family enjoyed the early 5K fun run and then we had a great time taking part in the parade, with flags waving overhead and the whole community lining the streets.
---
|
---
| |
During the parade, I high-fived more than 100 members of the community along the route. From excited kids outside the fire station with their candy bags to families gathered throughout town; the enthusiasm was contagious. The egg toss after the parade was a great highlight and there was a lot of excitement when two of our Team Baumgartner members placed in the final 3! Thank you, Rosalia, for the warm welcome and another great Battle Days celebration!
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| |
---
|
---
| |
# Celebrating Reardan Mule Days
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| |
---
| | | |

---
Team Baumgartner also attended this year’s Reardan Mule Days. Our team and volunteers had a great time walking in the parade, visiting with families, and connecting with neighbors throughout the day.

They even had the opportunity to catch up with State Representative Joe Schmick during the festivities. A special thank you to John and Jane who have graciously volunteered their truck for our summer parade season. I’m so grateful to our incredible volunteers and to the Reardan community for the warm welcome and continued support!
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/17kle2BjeCa?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238)
|
---
| |
# Volunteer Pizza Appreciation Night
---
|
---
| |
My team and I recently hosted a fun Volunteer Pizza Appreciation Night to celebrate the incredible dedication of our amazing team members. Our heartfelt thanks to everyone who has poured their time and energy into this campaign. From parade marches and door-knocking to making phone calls and jumping in at a moment’s notice, our volunteers are the heart of what we do. I am grateful for every volunteer who helps make this campaign successful!**Thank you all—we couldn’t do it without you!**
---
|
---
| |
# Volunteer Spotlight: Jackson
---
|
---
| | I want to extend a big thank you to Jackson, one of Team Baumgartner’s most faithful volunteers! Whether it is marching in parades, knocking on doors, or jumping in wherever help is needed, Jackson is always ready to roll up his sleeves.
His deep knowledge of the issues and willingness to speak with anyone is very much appreciated. He is an incredible asset to our team and true champion for our community! We’re grateful for his dedication and positive energy - thank you, Jackson, for all you do!

It was a wonderful opportunity to celebrate the red, white, and blue alongside our neighbors, honoring the freedoms and values that make our country so strong. The day was filled with patriotism, smiles, and a great sense of community pride. We loved being a part of this special tradition and want to thank the Fairfield organizers and everyone who came out to make the event so memorable! | | | | High-Fives and Hometown Spirit at Rosalia Battle Days! | | I loved being out at Rosalia Battle Days with my wife Eleanor, our kids, and great volunteers. Some members of the family enjoyed the early 5K fun run and then we had a great time taking part in the parade, with flags waving overhead and the whole community lining the streets. | | | During the parade, I high-fived more than 100 members of the community along the route. From excited kids outside the fire station with their candy bags to families gathered throughout town; the enthusiasm was contagious. The egg toss after the parade was a great highlight and there was a lot of excitement when two of our Team Baumgartner members placed in the final 3! Thank you, Rosalia, for the warm welcome and another great Battle Days celebration! | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Celebrating Reardan Mule Days | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Team Baumgartner also attended this year’s Reardan Mule Days. Our team and volunteers had a great time walking in the parade, visiting with families, and connecting with neighbors throughout the day. They even had the opportunity to catch up with State Representative Joe Schmick during the festivities. A special thank you to John and Jane who have graciously volunteered their truck for our summer parade season. I’m so grateful to our incredible volunteers and to the Reardan community for the warm welcome and continued support! | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Volunteer Pizza Appreciation Night | | | My team and I recently hosted a fun Volunteer Pizza Appreciation Night to celebrate the incredible dedication of our amazing team members. Our heartfelt thanks to everyone who has poured their time and energy into this campaign. From parade marches and door-knocking to making phone calls and jumping in at a moment’s notice, our volunteers are the heart of what we do. I am grateful for every volunteer who helps make this campaign successful!Thank you all—we couldn’t do it without you! | | | Volunteer Spotlight: Jackson | | | I want to extend a big thank you to Jackson, one of Team Baumgartner’s most faithful volunteers! Whether it is marching in parades, knocking on doors, or jumping in wherever help is needed, Jackson is always ready to roll up his sleeves. His deep knowledge of the issues and willingness to speak with anyone is very much appreciated. He is an incredible asset to our team and true champion for our community! We’re grateful for his dedication and positive energy - thank you, Jackson, for all you do! | | | We Need Your Help | | More campaign signs will be going up over these next few weeks. Will you host a yard sign? Click to sign up now, or just send an email reply!We need volunteers! If you have a couple of hours to spare, please reach out to us! Visit our ** to sign up now!Upcoming Events Our campaign is in full swing as Team Baumgartner travels across Eastern Washington connecting with communities and celebrating local traditions. Check out our next events and join us!Saturday June 20: Join Team Baumgartner at 10 am for Medical Lake Founders Day Parade in Spokane County. Founders Day brings neighbors together each year for a parade, local festivities, and family fun. Saturday June 20:**_ Join Team Baumgartner at 4 pm for Colville’s parade in Stevens County. This event brings together top professional rodeo athletes, thrilling competition, and classic parade fun that perfectly captures the Western spirit of our region. you for all your encouragement and support!-Michael | | | Paid for by Vote Baumgartner for Congress | www.votebaumgartner.com Our mailing address is: Vote Baumgartner for Congress, PO Box 8508, Spokane, WA 99203 | | | | | | | | | You can or | | |

I've known Jane Fonda for more than 50 years. We’ve shared movie sets and red carpets — but we’ve also shared picket lines, and even handcuffs on the steps of the Capitol for refusing to stay silent about the climate crisis. **I am proud to call her a dear friend. And I am even more proud of the work she and her team are doing right now at JanePAC. They remind me that change is still possible, and I’m reaching out today because they need our help.** What Donald Trump and his buddies are doing to this country isn't subtle anymore. They are consolidating power with ruthless efficiency, stacking every branch of government with allies, and rewarding the fossil fuel billionaires and corporate donors who scratch their backs while ordinary families are left to breathe the pollution and foot the bill. And yet, when I start to feel the weight of all of that, I think about Jane and this movement she has built. Since founding Jane Fonda Climate PAC, Jane and her team have helped elect over 240 climate champions from school boards to Congress who fight for our communities and can't be bought or bullied into silence. These last few weeks alone, JanePAC’s endorsed candidates won hard-fought primaries from California to Texas to Pennsylvania and beyond. These weren’t easy races. But they were able to invest in and support courageous leaders because grassroots supporters like you showed up. **So that's why I'm coming to you today. Jane's team set a goal to raise $35,000 by tomorrow night to power these final five months before November’s historic midterm elections, and I'm personally asking you to help them get there.** **[When we miss goals like this one, it means fewer resources for the candidates brave enough to stand up to Trump, Big Oil, and every powerful interest putting greed over our future. So whether it’s $10 or $25, your grassroots gift goes straight toward electing the next generation of leaders. strip virtually all meaningful protections for the national monument. But we’re still up against MAGA lawmakers in Congress: the Senate can still
advance this legislation through regular order. And on top of that, the House
could act on it at any time, then send it over to the Senate. This is not the
time to let down our defenses. Because if this legislation passes, it could create a roadmap for dismantling
protections for national monuments nationwide. We’re mounting a massive effort to keep pressure on EVERY member of Congress.Our Summer Membership Drive is underway and a group of donors has agreed to
triple match the first 5,000 membership contributions to the campaign. Will you pitch in? The best thing you can do to protect public lands right now is to renew your LCV membership. habitat. It’s home to bighorn sheep, mule deer, and endangered and protected

_Mohammed Al-Ali looking out from his balcony in the direction of Al-Hamidiya and his demolished home. June 9, 2026. Photo by Cian Ward._
QUNEITRA, Syria--Mohammed Al-Ali never got to celebrate the fall of Bashar al-Assad on December 8, 2024. It was the night his home was stolen by Israeli soldiers. As liberated civilians flooded the streets of Syria's cities in euphoria, the Israeli military burst into his home in the village of Al-Hamidiya and ordered Al-Ali and his family to leave.
"They barely gave us ten minutes to get out," Al-Ali, 50, told Drop Site News, teary-eyed as he recalled the night, clutching a cushion in his lap. "We weren't able to bring anything with us, we left our whole lives behind."
Al-Ali would never see his house again. Six months after his forced eviction, Israel demolished his home, alongside 15 others in Al-Hamidiya located in the Quneitra countryside of southwest Syria. According to a Syrian official, residents' reported that Israeli soldiers told them that the homes "blocked sight lines" from a newly constructed military base at the edge of the village. The official dismissed this pretext, saying "Israel uses the same justifications in Gaza and Lebanon."
Al-Ali's home had been built by his father. "That house was my life. It is where my children were born and raised," he explained, sitting in his grandparents' home in the nearby village of Jubat Al-Khashab. "They stole our home and our life. They stole our memories."
Over the last year, the new military base has been established on a hill overlooking Jubat Al-Khashab, where Al-Ali now lives. Residents are prohibited from approaching, and an Israeli drone whizzed into view within minutes of Drop Site photographing the base.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/97fe637f-9849-4647-a9a1-c2a00a3e6527?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
A new Israeli military base built on a hill overlooking Jubat Al-Khashab, Syria on June 9, 2026. Photo by Cian Ward.
The Israeli military has razed over 110 acres of ancient forest that once stood on the site. Farmers have been prohibited from accessing their fields nearby, and local residents reported incidents of animals that entered the vicinity around the base being seized.
The site has also become the launch point for Israeli raids on Jubat Al-Khashab. On June 7, five young men were snatched from their home just outside the village. Four were reportedly released after several hours of questioning, but one remains unaccounted for. A recent UN report, citing Syrian authorities, found that at least 250 Syrians have been arrested by Israel since 2024, with 50 still detained inside Israel.
The threat of being arrested and imprisoned in Israel--an illegal act under international law-- hangs like a specter over Quneitra.
Samar, 23, had snuck a local journalist onto the roof of Al-Hamidiya mosque to photograph the nearby Israeli military base in October 2025, when he noticed a resident looking at them and talking on the phone. Samar used a pseudonym to identify himself for security reasons.
Immediately, an Israeli convoy descended from the base. The journalist managed to escape, but Samar was caught. "The Israelis handcuffed and blindfolded me, pressed a gun to my head," he recalled.
They questioned him for several hours before finally letting him go. "They told me that if I ever see an Israeli patrol, I should turn and look away from them," he said. "If they catch me looking they would take me to the Golan and I would disappear."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/23e63e19-43ad-4516-a7c6-86ca6573c106?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The Golan Heights rising in the background amid haze from crop fires and mottled grasslands on June 9, 2026. Photo by Cian Ward.
The border region in southern Syria technically remains a UN-patrolled, demilitarized buffer zone established by the 1974 disengagement agreement that ended hostilities between Syria and Israel. However, following the ouster of Assad in 2024, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu unilaterally claimed this agreement had "collapsed" and ordered the Israeli military into Quneitra province from the Golan Heights, which were seized from Syria in 1967, and unilaterally annexed in 1981, a move unrecognised by the international community. Since then, Israel has deepened its occupation of Syria, establishing new positions in Quneitra, and occupying Jabal Al-Sheikh. Israel also launched a massive wave of airstrikes on Syria's military infrastructure in the days after Assad's fall, destroying its conventional military capability.
Israeli officials [claim](https://substack.com/redirect/1c9ae54c-fac3-444d-8352-59736cea9bf3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) without evidence that its raids target individuals linked to Hezbollah and other Iranian-linked groups. In April, Syria's Ministry of Interior arrested an alleged Hezbollah cell in Quneitra, and seized a mobile rocket launcher--the only notable instance of its kind.
Nevertheless, Syrian officials reject Israel's justification for occupation. "If Hezbollah cells do enter the province, our position is unambiguous," said a local official, speaking on the condition of anonymity. "It is the Syrian government's responsibility to arrest them and hold them to account, not Israel's."
"There is no social base for Hezbollah here, and so most of the arrests of local residents are baseless," he continued.
"These were areas of the revolution, why would we harbor Hezbollah?" said Hail Abdullah, the Mayor of Rasm Al-Rawadi, a village on the border that has had several homes demolished by the Israeli military. For years, Syria helped fund and arm Hezbollah, which intervened in 2013 in the country's civil war in defense of Bashar al-Assad. The group is opposed to Syria's new government under President Ahmed al-Sharaa, who has sought to ingratiate himself with President Donald Trump.
Abdullah explained how on December 8, the Israeli military gathered the residents of his village in the local school and ordered them to leave. "They said that they had come to clear Hezbollah from the region, and I replied, 'why now?'" he recounted. "If you had come at any point during the last 13-years we would have welcomed you, but now you intervene when the fighting is done?"
The countryside of Quneitra is a mottled yellow, as the long grass, fed by a year of heavy rain, dries in the sun. The air is hazy with the smoke of crop fires set by farmers, whose plumes dot the landscape intermittently.
In the 18 months since, the Israeli military has occupied the region. While Syrians said they rarely saw Israeli soldiers--who typically operate at night--they feel the military's presence constantly.
The most frequent reminder is the constant rumble of Israeli jets in the sky above. The Israelis target property, forcibly displacing residents and demolishing their homes. A [report](https://substack.com/redirect/59d93729-d3e0-4c2a-89b5-195109601b44?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by Amnesty International last month identified dozens of such cases, and found that the destruction of civilian homes should be investigated as war crimes. Equally, the report noted that destruction of property is "a hallmark of Israel's military operations in Gaza and Lebanon, and now in Syria."
Israel "seized Mantara dam, bulldozes farmland, and institutes grazing bans that make the countryside unworkable," said Nanar Hawach, senior researcher at the International Crisis Group. "Farmers who lose their fields often leave even when their homes are left standing."
"Israel is running its southern Lebanon model in Quneitra," he explained. In the latest phase of its war on Lebanon, Israel has invaded areas of southern Lebanon over the past three months, forcibly displacing some 60 towns and villages, designating them as no-go zones, and engaged in systematical, large-scale demolition of entire communities.
## **Under the Shadow of the Golan**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0616c898-331b-44ec-a238-174ea599218f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_Hala shows photos on her phone of the rubble that remains from her family home that the Israeli military demolished on June 6, 2026. Photo by Cian Ward._
Hala was staying with her mother in the Damascus countryside, when the Assad regime fell. She rushed to Assad's notorious Sednaya Prison in search of her husband who had gone missing in 2014. Her nephew, sent to check on her home in the village, which she asked not to be named, found it occupied by Israeli soldiers. "One of the soldiers was from Bab Touma [a neighbourhood in Damascus], he had left as a child in 1992," she said. "Now he has come back to take our land."
The day Assad fell, Hala "died twice". She found out that her husband wasn't in prison, so was most likely dead, and that the Israeli military had seized her home.
After several days, she went back to her village and "begged [the soldiers inside] to let me take my belongings." They ignored her as she sat outside her home for hours, clutching a white handkerchief she had been carrying, in the hope it would stop them shooting her. "A few days later they destroyed the home. I don't even know why."
The house she had lost was the third she had rebuilt. The previous two were destroyed during the Syrian civil war. She shows photos on her phone of the new kitchen she had installed only weeks before her eviction. "I paid 10 million lira [roughly $700] for it, but it's all gone," she sighed. "Now I am stuck living with my parents again, putting a burden on them."
Unlike Hala, Al-Ali hasn't returned to Al-Hamidiya since the eviction. He is too scared. "I've spoken to the media now, so if I go back they will probably arrest me," he said. Al-Ali's new residence is in Jubat Al-Khashab, a lush wooded village that sits under the shadow of the Golan Heights, whose buttress-like peaks are crowned by Israeli military bases.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/14c9f615-d2b7-4754-afdf-3f432b48972d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
A damaged mosque in Jubat Al-Khashab, with the Golan Heights in the background, crowned by several Israeli military posts and communication towers on June 9, 2026. Photo by Cian Ward.
Following Israel's seizure of the Golan Heights in 1967 war and unilateral annexation in 1981, large numbers of residents were expelled, many of whom resettled in Quneitra, as Israel began building settler outposts.
Israel's colonization of the Golan is ongoing. In April 2026, the Israeli cabinet approved plans to settle 3,000 new settler families in the occupied region by 2030.
Al-Ali's grandparents fled the Golan Heights and were never able to return. Ali "[doesn't] want to repeat the mistake of 1967 again," and so chose to remain in Quneitra, in his grandparents village, despite the presence of the Israeli military nearby.
"I was born here and I will die here," he said. "I don't want to feel the humiliation of being forced to leave this land."
In April, a large number of settlers, belonging to a group called the "Pioneers of Bashan"--a biblical term for southern Syria--occupied a building in the village of Al-Hader for several hours, singing songs and calling for the colonization of Quneitra. They were later removed by the Israeli military.
"They are attempting to repeat what they have done in the West Bank," said Hala, 42. "They destroy our homes and force us off our land so that they can claim them."

### Peter —
This week, we're going to Maine, where something historic just happened quietly and deserves to be said loudly. While Maine’s U.S Senate primary has been a focal point recently with party candidates Graham Platner and Susan Collins occupying headlines, the Governor's race has brought voters’ optimism back to their state. We’re featuring [Rick Bennett](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=DrBycgz7v9R4FAsTJPsPn6ftsXuiPKFVAH_Sil4QV48&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_105a&n=1) this week - Bennett is a Harvard-educated businessman, a former President of the Maine State Senate, and a lifelong Republican who spent decades building his party — then walked away from it. On June 24, 2025, he announced he would run for governor as an independent, ending a party affiliation he'd held his entire political life. Just a couple weeks ago, he qualified for the November gubernatorial ballot — **the only independent to do so.** Here is the argument most independent candidates have to make:_I'll find a way to work with everyone once I get there._ Rick Bennett doesn't have to try to make that argument - he already has the record proving that he can. He has spent 18 years in the Maine Legislature doing exactly what he is now asking Maine voters to elect him do in the Blaine House. He has built coalitions, negotiated with Democrats and Republicans, moved legislation through a divided chamber, and delivered results on the issues Maine families actually talk about at the kitchen table. **This is not a candidate learning on the job.** This is a candidate who has already done the job, at every level of the legislative process, and who is now asking for the chance to do it from the top. ___ The Maine governor's race has gone to a ranked-choice runoff, with results expected before June 19th. On the GOP side, with 43% of votes counted Tuesday night, Bobby Charles — an attorney who ran a Trump-style campaign largely relying on social media — led with more than 38%. No candidate crossed the 50% threshold, sending the Republican primary to a ranked-choice runoff that will conclude before June 19th. Ben Midgley and Jonathan Bush were neck-and-neck for second place. The Democratic field is even less clear, with Nirav Shah, Hannah Pingree, Troy Jackson, and Shenna Bellows all within 6% of each other. Who comes out of that field is anyone's guess. But one thing is clear - Rick is the only candidate who is ready to win in November. **Maine loves its independents, having elected two independent governors in its modern history: James Longley, who served from 1975 to 1979, and U.S. Sen. Angus King, who served as governor from 1995 to 2003 before being elected to the Senate.** Rick was the first candidate that the Forward Party endorsed for the 2026 cycle in December of 2025. He’s the right leader for Maine, and we’re proud to support his campaign. To learn more about Rick, [check out his website here](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=DrBycgz7v9R4FAsTJPsPn6ftsXuiPKFVAH_Sil4QV48&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_105a&n=2)! **Please forward this to your friends, family, and coworkers. It helps us introduce them to Forward and to what we are building. Also consider inviting them to one of our upcoming events listed below. We'd love to meet them.**

clean_body: But not the race you think! | | | www.forwardparty.com Peter — This week, we're going to Maine, where something historic just happened quietly and deserves to be said loudly. While Maine’s U.S Senate primary has been a focal point recently with party candidates Graham Platner and Susan Collins occupying headlines, the Governor's race has brought voters’ optimism back to their state. We’re featuring this week - Bennett is a Harvard-educated businessman, a former President of the Maine State Senate, and a lifelong Republican who spent decades building his party — then walked away from it. On June 24, 2025, he announced he would run for governor as an independent, ending a party affiliation he'd held his entire political life. Just a couple weeks ago, he qualified for the November gubernatorial ballot — the only independent to do so. Here is the argument most independent candidates have to make:I'll find a way to work with everyone once I get there. Rick Bennett doesn't have to try to make that argument - he already has the record proving that he can. He has spent 18 years in the Maine Legislature doing exactly what he is now asking Maine voters to elect him do in the Blaine House. He has built coalitions, negotiated with Democrats and Republicans, moved legislation through a divided chamber, and delivered results on the issues Maine families actually talk about at the kitchen table. This is not a candidate learning on the job. This is a candidate who has already done the job, at every level of the legislative process, and who is now asking for the chance to do it from the top. _ The Maine governor's race has gone to a ranked-choice runoff, with results expected before June 19th. On the GOP side, with 43% of votes counted Tuesday night, Bobby Charles — an attorney who ran a Trump-style campaign largely relying on social media — led with more than 38%. No candidate crossed the 50% threshold, sending the Republican primary to a ranked-choice runoff that will conclude before June 19th. Ben Midgley and Jonathan Bush were neck-and-neck for second place. The Democratic field is even less clear, with Nirav Shah, Hannah Pingree, Troy Jackson, and Shenna Bellows all within 6% of each other. Who comes out of that field is anyone's guess. But one thing is clear - Rick is the only candidate who is ready to win in November. Maine loves its independents, having elected two independent governors in its modern history: James Longley, who served from 1975 to 1979, and U.S. Sen. Angus King, who served as governor from 1995 to 2003 before being elected to the Senate. Rick was the first candidate that the Forward Party endorsed for the 2026 cycle in December of 2025. clean_body: Peter, I'm going to make a prediction... When the votes are counted this November, the radical left is going to be in a state of total shock. And the political establishment is going to spend weeks trying to explain what hit them. But that only happens if Republicans like you are on record before the Midterms. That is how consequential this moment is. But here is the part the pundits won't tell you. None of that happens automatically. The Democrats are at war with the American people -- open borders, defunding ICE, eliminating voter ID, putting men in women's sports. You name it, they are on the wrong side of it. And yet they are running the most radical, well-funded Senate candidates in states across this country who are counting on Republicans to stay home and let them walk right in. I will not let that happen. And I don't think you will either. I made you a prediction at the beginning of this email. I stand by every word of it. But that prediction is built on one assumption -- that Republicans like you are engaged and ready to fight. That is where your assessment comes in. Team,
Not only has Dan Meuser never held a real town hall, he can't even be bothered to pick up the phone for his constituents.
The owner of a local daycare center said that [she tried to contact Dan](https://substack.com/redirect/0024947f-7e4e-4076-bd90-05a6987b8a6f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) about the planned 7,500-person ICE detention center that would open right next to her business:
> _" I left messages, voicemails. I sent emails out. And no response."_
That's unacceptable.
Dan has promised that the two mega-ICE detention centers coming to our district will have a "positive impact" here. Despite the fact that our communities don't have the drinking water, emergency services capacity, or local infrastructure to support them. The sewage system in Tremont would be so overwhelmed that it would take **150 poop trucks** to haul the waste out.
**Over 100 people came to a town hall I held about the detention centers. People here are saying it loud and clear:**_**we don 't want this.**_**We cannot accept being ignored by our representative.**
DHS is appealing the pause on these facilities. This isn't over. If Dan Meuser won't take our side, or even answer our questions about this, then he needs to go.

We deserve better than this.
Thank you,
Rachel Wallace

| | Peter, **The federal tax code runs tens of thousands of pages. Not one of them was written to help you.** Every line was built to grow Washington, fund the bureaucracy, and squeeze working families a little harder every year.I have had enough, and I think you have too. **That is why I support the FairTax Act.** Scrap the IRS, simplify the whole broken system, and let working Alabamians keep more of what they earn. Simple. Fair. Long overdue. The career politicians will tell you it cannot be done. They say that because the current system works just fine for them and their donors. It does not work for the family in Dothan stretching a paycheck, or the small business owner in Monroeville drowning in compliance costs. It works against them. I did not come up through that system, and I do not owe it anything. I came up as a Green Beret, where the mission is the mission and excuses do not count. I will bring that same standard to Washington.But I need your help to get there. subject: Renaming the Department of Defense
body:
One of the basic rules in economics and finance is to watch out for what you're spending. Spend wisely, invest smartly, and plan for the future. You know the drill. But it seems the people we elect to represent us in Washington D.C. slept through that lecture. Ronny Jackson, illustrious in his posturing and steadfastly superglued to Donald Trump's side, recently offered up an amendment to a bill to officially rename the Department of Defense to the Department of War. (For those elected types

| | | One of the basic rules in economics and finance is to watch out for what you're spending. Spend wisely, invest smartly, and plan for the future. You know the drill.But it seems the people we elect to represent us in Washington D.C. slept through that lecture.Ronny Jackson, illustrious in his posturing and steadfastly superglued to Donald Trump's side, recently [offered up an amendment to a bill](https://blog.marknair.com/r/aef1eb25?m=11bd26bf-89d8-44d0-9794-5184de65ec00) to officially [rename the Department of Defense](https://blog.marknair.com/r/b5631a38?m=11bd26bf-89d8-44d0-9794-5184de65ec00) to the Department of War.(_For those elected types who are deficient in their American history, the name Department of Defense happened during Truman 's presidency when he consolidated all the different military into one unified department. _[_Truman described it this way_](https://blog.marknair.com/r/41d5a723?m=11bd26bf-89d8-44d0-9794-5184de65ec00) _:_
> "It means a concentration and cohesion of our best military thought and our best military resources, geared to maximum efficiency. It means using our experience in World War II for the peace of the world."
_The peace of the world. American used to be the vanguard of that noble idea.__Now, not so much._)But back to wise spending. These guys harp and crow about inefficiency and waste, but it's all a cover, a smokescreen to hide their very own incompetence and drunken spending. This Department of Defense name change alone could cost $125 million dollars.$125 million dollars to make a few pathetic men feel tough.And that's just an estimate of cost. It's the government, after all, and nothing gets by cheaply. Here's what the the [Congressional Budget Office estimates:](https://blog.marknair.com/r/f0c576ff?m=11bd26bf-89d8-44d0-9794-5184de65ec00)
> Costs would be at least a few million dollars if DoD phased in a
> minimal implementation, but they could be as large as $125 million if the
> name change was implemented broadly and rapidly throughout the
> department. A statutory renaming could cost hundreds of millions of dollars depending on how Congress and DoD chose to implement the change.
This amendment is exactly that: a statutory renaming. And it could cost **hundreds of millions of dollars**.Of your money.These people might be terrible at their jobs. Incompetent at representing people. Disasters at running an economy. But they're very good at wasting your money. They're very good at abusing their offices and their authority.This is what I want to stop.|
* * *
|
---
Every so often I see another cry from our electeds, promoting how terrific and wonderful they are on combating fraud and waste. Ronny Jackson, is one of those who beats his chest at the slightest appearance of doing _something_ , anything, so he can post about it.
This time it's [House Bill 1335](https://blog.marknair.com/r/26873af5?m=11bd26bf-89d8-44d0-9794-5184de65ec00). It's a non-binding resolution that condemns government fraud. Here's the relevant part of the resolution:
> Resolved, That the House of Representatives--
> (1) condemns the fraudulent actions of those seeking to defraud the United States Government;
> (2) believes government wide fraud and improper payment prevention legislative and policy reforms will meaningfully improve the continued financial prosperity of the United States Government and the American taxpayer; and
> (3) believes Federal program eligibility and spending activities should be verified prior to payments being issued.
Let me stress this. It's not a law. It's nothing. It's just a resolution that goes nowhere and has authority over nothing. It doesn't fund a thing. It doesn't answer a question. It solves nothing. That's what our lawmakers are doing with their time and the salaries you pay them. They condemn and believe. They urge and suggest.
We're in a war. Life is too expensive. We're jeopardizing our futures by massively investing in technology that will destroy jobs.
And this is the kind of non-action and pathetic "legislation" that takes up their day.
Really, though, condemning fraud with real action would be terrific. So let's do it. And we will after this November's election when we kick out the hucksters, fraudsters, con men, child abusers, predators, sycophants, and toadies who care nothing for you but look out for only themselves.

I'm old enough to have witnessed the life and actions of Mother Teresa, and how she inspired everyone from Popes and Princesses to see Christ in every human being. A profound but curious, deeply complex retort of hers when people, full of good intentions, would offer to go to India and help her work. "Find your own Calcutta". The meaning: one need not venture to the other side of the world to do good. One can, in fact must, do it right where he is.
This is a stark difference between true Christian Charity and popular secular humanism. It is easier to do good when the needy are distant. "Remote" would be a better word. Or even "removed". The untouchables of India. The famine victims in Ethiopia. The starving children in wherever.
Mother was quietly and politely but firmly saying "I know you're not going to come to India, but I'm not going to call you out publicly, so I will redirect your newfound virtue to a more manageable location." Or, the axiom, "charity starts at home".
If you want to run a marathon, buying new sneakers feels like the start of the process, but running a 5k after work IS a start. How many times we have bought the sneakers. I know I have. The sneakers. The rowing machine. The 5 easy steps to a six pack. Breaking a sweat is the hard part.

Not because they have found a crime, but because they are simply trying to find one.

**Trump's Department of Justice is investigating me.**
In recent days, federal agents have knocked on the doors of family, friends, and former employees.
Not because they have found a crime, but because they are simply trying to find one.
They are demanding records.
They are digging through years and years of random documents.
They are abusing the grand jury process.
They are doing to me -- and my wife -- what they did to Jerome Powell, James Comey, Tish James, Adam Schiff, the six members of Congress who made a video he didn't like, and a woman a jury found Donald Trump had sexually abused.
Now it's my turn.
Not because I do mean tweets, but because I am considering running for president.
He is simply the most corrupt president in American history.
Last year, when Trump illegally deployed the National Guard and United States Marines to the streets of California, he called for my arrest.
Now his Department of Justice is trying to carry out his wishes.
Fighting back will require a legal strategy and a political strategy, and, unfortunately, I am going to need your help on both -- and one of the most important things you can do today (besides spreading the word), is making a contribution to support that effort.

body:
https://rokhanna.com [https://rokhanna.com]
Peter,
Cyrus Belton was 14 years old. He was shot from behind while running away. The man who killed him was acquitted.
For many Black Americans, the acquittal in this case reopened wounds that stretch across generations and raised painful questions about justice, accountability, and the value placed on Black life.
From Trayvon Martin to Tamir Rice, the names change, but the questions remain.
Karmelo Anthony, a Black teenager who was bullied, was convicted last week not of manslaughter, but of first-degree murder. He was sentenced to 35 years in prison.
Many are left asking what these vastly different outcomes reveal about accountability, race, and the way justice is experienced in America.
I’m calling for three key reforms that courts can take right now to counter this dangerous disparity:
* Strengthen public defense and access to legal counsel, regardless of income
* Assign independent prosecutors in controversial cases
* Establish an independent commission to examine racial disparities in the justice system
Sign if you agree: We need judicial reform NOW. name: Britney VanCitters
subject: Tell Your Legislators: Every Oregonian Deserves the Right to Cooling
body:
https://secure.ngpvan.com/EhX8aWdsuUmUlS88s_Sfbg2?contactdata=+9nnSHv1lUXqy8GDR4PrGfWHiQVT5VDhoXntSyPQley8gJ9wdSuhh9AevQra5EiHJ7Cwd8rTuRGiNPLU5Ei793TioqcconuAtZnO6DZh9gF2NiagwPl74DhIpOy88884 [https://secure.ngpvan.com/EhX8aWdsuUmUlS88s_Sfbg2?contactdata=+9nnSHv1lUXqy8GDR4PrGfWHiQVT5VDhoXntSyPQley8gJ9wdSuhh9AevQra5EiHJ7Cwd8rTuRGiNPLU5Ei793TioqcconuAtZnO6DZh9gF2NiagwPl74DhIpOy88884]
Hi Peter,
This weekend was warm. As the days get hotter, I’m reminded of the damaging Heat Dome 5 years ago this month. It was a wake-up call that not only took lives and made people sick, but harmed the food supply and scorched our beloved forests.
Extreme heat due to climate change is no longer a future threat. It's here, and it's becoming one of the greatest risks to the health and safety of Oregon communities. Will you take action for the right to cooling for all? [https://secure.ngpvan.com/EhX8aWdsuUmUlS88s_Sfbg2]
Heat is now the deadliest natural disaster in the United States. Oregon is experiencing more dangerous heat days than ever before. Yet too many Oregonians, especially people with low incomes, seniors, people with disabilities, rural communities, and communities of color, still don't have access to the cooling they need to stay safe.
We believe every Oregonian has a Right to Cooling, which is a Right to Live. [https://secure.ngpvan.com/EhX8aWdsuUmUlS88s_Sfbg2]
Take action [https://secure.ngpvan.com/EhX8aWdsuUmUlS88s_Sfbg2?contactdata=+9nnSHv1lUXqy8GDR4PrGfWHiQVT5VDhoXntSyPQley8gJ9wdSuhh9AevQra5EiHJ7Cwd8rTuRGiNPLU5Ei793TioqcconuAtZnO6DZh9gF2NiagwPl74DhIpOy88884]
Our homes and buildings are our first line of defense against extreme heat. While cooling shelters and emergency air conditioner deployments save lives in the short term, Oregon must invest in lasting solutions that help people stay safe year after year. Heat pumps provide cooling in the summer, efficient heating in the winter, and can lower utility bills, making them one of the most effective tools for building resilience.
Access to cooling doesn’t just make living more comfortable, but it saves lives.
Oregon has stepped up before. After the deadly 2021 Heat Dome, lawmakers created statewide heat pump incentive programs and strengthened tenant protections. But since 2025, key resilience programs—including heat pump incentives for homeowners and renters, the Healthy Homes Program, and Community Resilience Hubs—have been defunded, leaving many Oregonians with few options to protect themselves from extreme heat.
As burning fossil fuels drives hotter summers, Oregon must renew its commitment to resilience. We need investments that prioritize those most vulnerable to extreme heat, expand access to cooling and weatherization upgrades, and ensure that polluters help pay for the climate impacts they're causing. Legislative Days are happening now, and lawmakers need to hear from you before they meet to discuss extreme heat.
Will you take a minute to email your legislators and tell them that every Oregonian deserves the right to cooling? [https://secure.ngpvan.com/EhX8aWdsuUmUlS88s_Sfbg2]
Send your message today and urge lawmakers to:
* Invest in heat pump and weatherization incentive programs.
* Restore funding for community resilience initiatives.
* Prioritize vulnerable communities in resilience investments.
* Make polluters pay for the climate harms driving extreme heat.
Your voice matters on this topic so much now. For Legislative Days legislators are meeting in the Capitol this week to hold hearings on specific topics. One of those topics is Extreme Heat, [https://secure.ngpvan.com/EhX8aWdsuUmUlS88s_Sfbg2?contactdata=+9nnSHv1lUXqy8GDR4PrGfWHiQVT5VDhoXntSyPQley8gJ9wdSuhh9AevQra5EiHJ7Cwd8rTuRGiNPLU5Ei793TioqcconuAtZnO6DZh9gF2NiagwPl74DhIpOy88884] so sending your message now will only get them talking more! clean_body: Attorneys general are a critical frontline of defense against MAGA corruption | = Hey Peter, it’s Letitia James. As attorney general of New York, I know firsthand what it takes to serve in this critical office in the midst of MAGA chaos. And I’ll be blunt: It’s not easy. I know what it means to stand up to Donald Trump and his allies — and I know what it means to become a target when you do. Last year, after I held Trump accountable for his corruption, his Justice Department came after me. But I didn’t back down. And neither can any of us. Trump and his allies have shown us again and again that they will stop at nothing to peddle their corrupt agenda, manipulate the justice system, and attack anyone who stands in their way. That’s why attorneys general are a critical line of defense to fight back against MAGA corruption in the states. And it’s why I’m proud to support my friends Nicole Cannizzaro in Nevada and Tanya Miller in Georgia — two women ready to take on Republican extremism and serve as their states' next attorneys general. = | = Nicole Cannizzaro is a lifelong Nevadan who spent 11 years as a prosecutor taking on scammers, abusers, and criminals to keep her community safe. She is now the majority leader of the Nevada state Senate, where she has led tough fights to codify the right to choose, increase funding for public schools, and deliver for working families. Tanya Miller is a Georgia state representative with more than two decades of courtroom experience. Tanya has spent her career fighting for victims, workers, and families — and as Georgia’s next attorney general, she will bring that same commitment to justice to protect her constituents from violence, corruption, and abuse. I know what these offices demand. I know the courage it takes to stand up to powerful people who think the rules do not apply to them. And I know that Nicole and Tanya are exactly the kind of leaders we need for this moment. They are no strangers to tough fights, and they will work tirelessly to uphold the rule of law — no matter what Trump and his cronies may throw their way. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue, your donation will go through immediately: = | = ---|--- = | = = | = Nicole and Tanya are the women for the job, Peter. Peter, I'm reaching

and I need you with us.

What’s happening in our country right now is not normal. Trump is
targeting anyone who stands in his way. Immigrants living, working, and
raising families here are being ripped from their homes. Voting rights are
being dismantled to benefit the MAGA movement. Working people are drowning
while the wealthy write the rules.

This is no accident. It’s a choice.
And we have a choice too.

I have always believed that the people closest to the pain are closest to
the power to heal it. That's not just a saying, it's the foundation of
everything Alexandria, Ilhan, Rashida, and I have built together.

We didn't arrive in Congress on our own. We were carried here by
communities, by organizers, by people who refused to accept that this is
just the way things are.

That's you — and this movement you've helped build.

The Squad Victory Fund exists because collective action is how we win. Not
one leader, not one election — but all of us, together, making sure the
people who refuse to sell out have what they need to keep fighting.

We don't take corporate money. We don't answer to PACs or billionaires.
Our power comes from one place: people like you deciding that this moment
is worth showing up for.

Tonight is one of those moments. We have a mid-month deadline, and hitting
it matters. It means we can keep organizing, keep building, and keep
fighting for the future our communities deserve.

meet this goal, we stay in the fight — and that's exactly where we intend
to be.
